📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, editor's note - This article's headline previously claimed that this ongoing discount represented a new lowest-ever price for the Google Pixel 10. That is not the case, as the handset was previously discounted to $534 in June 2026, and the article has been updated to reflect this.

Black Friday is the best time to upgrade your flagship smartphone without breaking the bank, as prices keep going up. Google’s regular flagship has to be a contender if you want a small Android phone with good cameras and useful software.

According to recent reports, right now, the unlocked Google Pixel 10 is on sale at Amazon for $593, down from its usual price of $799. That's 26% off, saving you over $200 and tying the lowest price we've seen for this model since mid-July. You’ll want to act fast, though, as this deal is live only while supplies last.

Sources indicate that the Pixel 10 combines Google's software experience with practical AI features, a versatile triple-camera system, and a bright OLED display. At under $599, you're getting a phone that originally launched at $799 for considerably less.

✅ Recommended if: You’re an average smartphone user, an iPhone switcher or a budget buyer who likes clean software, useful AI features and a simple design.

❌ Skip this deal if: You’re a heavy mobile gamer, a videographer, a power user who hates slow charging, or you own a recent Pixel already.

In a recent development, the Pixel 10 isn't trying too hard to be different, with a 6.3-inch screen and a design that's pretty much "business as usual." The software experience is clean and a substantial part of the appeal, especially if you prefer Google's take on Android over heavily customized interfaces. It's also worth considering if you're thinking of moving away from an iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that one of the phone’s big selling points is its triple rear-camera setup, which adds a 5x telephoto lens with up to 20x Super Res Zoom. You also get Google’s Tensor G5 processor and 12GB of RAM, along with software features meant to make everyday tasks more convenient. That stated, the Tensor G5 isn't particularly powerful for demanding workloads, so heavy gamers may want to look elsewhere.

According to recent reports, the numbers make the device a more interesting deal. It has a 6.3-inch Actua OLED panel with a 120Hz refresh rate and peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits. Google claims you’ll get over 24 hours of battery life, and the Qi2 Pixelsnap magnetic wireless charger is yet another handy convenience. The phone is also IP68 water and dust resistant and has Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2 protection.

According to recent reports, of course, $599 doesn’t mean the Pixel 10 is without compromises. You get downgraded main and ultrawide camera sensors, slow charging speeds and buggy software updates that can make the experience frustrating. If raw performance, fast charging or heavy-duty video work are what you are after, the Pixel 10 isn't the phone we'd recommend.

Following the last release 11 months ago, Google is rolling out the first update of 2026 to the Chromecast with Google TV (4K).

It has been revealed that enhancement 11/23: The UTTA.260813.002 Chromecast with Google TV update is now seeing wide availability. This was a strange rollout.

On your Chromecast with Google TV, go to Settings > System > About > System update to download and install.

GrapheneOS indicates off how it looks RCS support without Google Messages

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (300 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • RCS is coming to GrapheneOS without Google Messages, as a proof-of-concept app highlights how the privacy-focused version Android can implement the messaging standard.
  • Recent findings suggest that as virtually all Android phones and now iPhone support RCS messaging, the standard is key to communication in 2026.
  • It’s a problem that Graphene’s developers have been trying to work out for a while now, and it seems progress is being made.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RCS is coming to GrapheneOS without Google Messages, as a proof-of-concept app highlights how the privacy-focused version Android can implement the messaging standard.

Recent findings suggest that as virtually all Android phones and now iPhone support RCS messaging, the standard is key to communication in 2026. But GrapheneOS users, by default, are still stuck with SMS/MMS as RCS is typically locked behind Google Messages on Android.

It’s a problem that Graphene’s developers have been trying to work out for a while now, and it seems progress is being made. A proof-of-concept messaging app with RCS was shared on Twitter/X, showing Graphene’s RCS implementation working with both Google Messages and iOS with end-to-end encryption and full features including typing indicators and reactions.

While this app skips the need to use Google Messages directly, the app does still use Google’s services as most carriers rely on Google for RCS. GrapheneOS still needs a sandboxed version of Google Play, for now, for this to work, but the developers say that a standalone version for carriers that support Google-less RCS will be coming.

In a recent development, we made a proof of concept RCS messaging app. It already has end-to-end encryption with MLS compatible with Google Messages and iOS, typing indicators, delivery/read receipts, reactions and media/file sharing. We'll use what was learned to integrate RCS into our Messaging app. pic.twitter.com/jzCTCCKrIQ.

There’s still no firm timeline for this fresh RCS support on GrapheneOS, but Google Messages can still be used in the meantime.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Following the Gemini app, Google Wallet integration is coming to AI Mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Personal Intelligence in AI Mode is expanding today with Google Drive, Wallet, and even Gemini app integrations.

Sources indicate that before today’s announcement, Personal Intelligence in AI Mode supported Google Photos and Workspace (Gmail and Calendar). This is used to customize responses based on your data. The new Google Drive support lets AI Mode take into account your Docs, Sheets, and PDFs.

Following the Gemini app, Google Wallet integration is coming to AI Mode. On the safety front, AI Mode can only read information from your financial accounts. It cannot “move, manage, or invest your money.”.

…you can map out your financial milestones and identify actionable ways to trim everyday spending. You can also maximize credit card benefits — like optimizing cash-back categories, travel perks, and reward points — based on your cards linked via Wallet.

The last integration today is the most interesting. You will be able to “securely connect your Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode.”.

…if you explore an idea in the Gemini app, AI Mode will have that foundation to build on, and vice versa.

This builds on the existing ability to have the Gemini app factor your Search history into answers. With this update, AI Mode can access “your Gemini chats, what you’ve shared with Gemini Apps (like photos, files, audio or video attachments, and screens you ask about), and associated insights and locations.” The option to make the connection is available today, but the feature will go live in the coming weeks.

You can control Personal Intelligence in AI Mode from this page.

Google will soon show a “Personalization” icon below tailored responses that lets you “view the context AI Mode uses.”.

The final upgrade today will make AI Overviews and AI Mode responses “more personally relevant.”.

According to recent reports, so if you’ve been researching and planning for a trip, you can pick up right where you left off in a new search thread without starting over or repeating yourself. As always, you can adjust or turn off personalization at any time in your Search Settings.

Google Meet unlocks 1080p video streaming for all accounts on web

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Streaming in 1080p will be the default in Google Meet, regardless of whether you pay for Google Workspace.
  • Google states customers will default to sending and receiving 1080p video, at the minimum.
  • According to recent reports, the upgrade will roll out to everyone, including those with Google Workspace accounts and personal Google Accounts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Streaming in 1080p will be the default in Google Meet, regardless of whether you pay for Google Workspace. That includes personal Google Accounts.

Google states customers will default to sending and receiving 1080p video, at the minimum. Previously, Google Meet made 720p the standard for streaming, and a higher resolution had historically been locked behind the Google One 2TB plan. That’s been true since 1080p streaming was rolled out in 2023.

According to recent reports, the upgrade will roll out to everyone, including those with Google Workspace accounts and personal Google Accounts. The only requirement to stream your own 1080p video in Google Meet for web will be hardware-based. Google’s press release states that devices with cameras capable of streaming in high definition will do so, and the feature will be turned on automatically.

Sources indicate that it can be disabled, though. Consumers can head to Settings > Video in Google Meet for web. Video will also appear in a lower resolution if the user’s video tile is shrunk down on-screen.

Industry observers note that the enhancement appears to be centered on web-only instances of Google Meet, and might not include the app on Android or iOS. For the time being, those versions may still be limited to streaming in 720p for those who don’t have an active Google One subscription.

Google Meet started its extended rollout of 1080p streaming to everyone earlier this month, so it shouldn’t be much longer until the change has taken place completely.

  • It has been revealed that by the time December arrives, stepping outside might feel like taking a cold plunge.
  • According to recent reports, updated November 27, 2026: More walking pad and running treadmill deals were added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday is officially here, and plenty of great deals are live. Several walking pads are currently marked down, and with winter coming, now is the ideal time to take advantage of the discount. I, for one, have already started prepping my hibernation cave by stocking happy lights, arts and crafts, and a brand-new walking pad.

It has been revealed that by the time December arrives, stepping outside might feel like taking a cold plunge. At that point, you’ll wish you had snagged a walking pad sooner to help you reach your step count goals without risking frostbite. Below, get a curated list of walking pad treadmills I have tested and vetted that are on sale.

According to recent reports, updated November 27, 2026: More walking pad and running treadmill deals were added. Prices and links were also updated.

It has been revealed that the Urevo CyberPad is my favorite walking pad, and it’s on sale for $390 ($110 off). I’m confident in the product’s durability, mainly due to its sturdy-feeling build and comfortable belt. It offers a 14-percent incline, which is one of the highest available in walking pads, and the speed tops out at 4 mph. Unfortunately, the incline capability makes the machine difficult to store under furniture. It weighs about 71 pounds, so moving it around isn’t fun, but the wheels help. You can control the CyberPad with its remote control and companion app. You can also view your real-time metrics on the machine’s display.

Sources indicate that the Urevo Strol 2S Pro is also on sale for $210 off. This 2-in-1 doubles as a treadmill with adjustable handrails, a display, and an attachable tablet holder. It was simple to set up, complete with a remote control and intuitive companion app. It feels super stable underfoot, even at top speed and incline level (7.6 mph and 9 percent). That top speed likely isn’t fast enough if you’re looking to sprint, but it’s plenty for a good workout. The machine is unobtrusive, has a quiet motor, and the 43-inch track is compact enough to place under your desk. Overall, it’s a sturdy walking pad treadmill that offers great value and range.

It has been revealed that the WalkingPad C2 Foldable Walking Treadmill’s track is 32.5 inches when folded (and unfurls to 57 inches), making it a great option for storage in small spaces. It weighs 62 pounds, which isn’t light, but it makes for a sturdier running deck and a (hopefully) longer lifespan. You can adjust the speed via the remote control or companion app. Reviewer Kristin Canning found the app itself to be a little wonky. For example, if you don’t start a workout within the app, your data won’t sync. The app also saves each walking session separately, so if you take a break, you start from zero again. The good news is you don’t need to use the app to use the walking pad.

Canning also didn’t like that when you first start using the machine, you have to walk at slower speeds before you can unlock the upper end of the range. This might appeal to folks who enjoy gamifying their workouts, though. The app also offers workout programs that auto-adjust the speed to your pace via sensors under the belt.

The industry’s biggest players are joining together to celebrate all the amazing VR games you probably don’t know about (but should).

This year has been difficult for the gaming industry at large, and that’s particularly true for the wonderful niche of VR gaming. Despite some huge setbacks, VR gaming is still alive and well, popping out tons of amazing games this year that you may not have realized. To celebrate those wins, VR studio and publishing label Creature is joined by Future Friends Games to bring back the VR Forever Awards this December.

Sources indicate that throughout the entire festival, you can expect tons of fresh game demos on Steam, including over 220 games from nearly 150 developers. While the festival is technically on Steam, Meta Quest still rules the roost in the VR world, so you can expect plenty of surprises for Quest gamers.

According to recent reports, the festival will run from December 3rd to 9th on Steam and will cover the best of VR across six categories: Best Hidden Gem, Best Single Player, Best Multiplayer, Best Ongoing, Most Anticipated Game, and Game of the Year. This year’s judges include Zeena Al-Obaidi (CCO at VR Games Showcase), Ian Hamilton (Founder of Good Virtual Reality), Naysy (Content Creator, VR Forever Ambassador), and Nicholas Sutrich (me!).

Sources indicate that the full list of winners and nominees will be confirmed during the show, but Creature highlights Forefront, Thief VR: Legacy of Shadow, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Empire City, Dungeons of Eternity, Titan Isles, and the ever-popular Hot Dogs, Horseshoes & Hand Grenades 2 as some of the most notable. Visit the VR Forever website to learn more, and check out Naysy’s video above for even more details!

Breaking: Scam Roblox cheat codes are injecting malware into computers, reports reveal

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kids looking for an easy edge in Roblox may be giving scammers access to the whole family computer.
  • Recent findings suggest that A Cybernews investigation found that Roblox generated more than 22 million cheat-related searches from 2018 to 2026.
  • With some context, it's understandable why Roblox makes for an easy target.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kids looking for an easy edge in Roblox may be giving scammers access to the whole family computer.

Recent findings suggest that A Cybernews investigation found that Roblox generated more than 22 million cheat-related searches from 2018 to 2026. That's more than half of all the cheat searches across the 17 major games the outlet tracked. Security researchers working at Cybernews say scammers are using that demand to pass off malware as working cheats.

With some context, it's understandable why Roblox makes for an easy target. The platform is free to download, but many of the games inside it put weapons, VIP perks, and rare items behind paywalls. Those usually cost between $5 and $50, according to Cybernews. That has led to a steady stream of stories about kids running up charges on a parent's credit card, and the RobloxHelp subreddit is full of parents asking how to get their money back.

"Kids without access to credit cards look to cut corners on YouTube and Google search," Cybernews writes in its report.

In a recent development, no other game in Cybernews' study came close. Over the past 12 months, Roblox drew nearly 3.9 million cheat searches. Counter-Strike 2 came in second with about 533,000. Adjusted for player count, Roblox gets 482 cheat searches per 1,000 players, more than six times Minecraft's rate.

Recent findings suggest that many Roblox cheats rely on script executors — third-party programs that let players run their own code inside Roblox games. Antivirus software routinely flags these tools, so young players have gotten used to clicking past Windows Defender warnings, according to Cybernews. Many also hand full administrator access to unverified files they found through YouTube videos and Discord servers. Back in March, a threat actor listed 50 million allegedly stolen Roblox logins for sale. Cybernews claims they were likely collected by password-stealing malware running on infected devices.

A few months later, in August, security firm Bitdefender uncovered a campaign spreading fake "undetected" versions of Xeno, a popular Roblox executor, Cybernews reported. The downloads came with real cheat scripts so they'd appear to work, but also contained malware. That malware could steal Roblox logins, saved browser passwords, and Discord accounts. It could also record keystrokes and even capture webcam footage.

Recent findings suggest that these kinds of scams are even riskier if Roblox is played on a shared computer. If a child uses the same computer their parents use, malware can steal a parent's saved banking logins, work email, and personal files, too.

It has been revealed that last year, Check Point Research found a similar scheme aimed at Minecraft players. Fake mods posing as the popular cheat tools Oringo and Taunahi were spread through malicious GitHub repositories. They infected more than 1,500 devices starting in March 2025, TechSpot reported. The malware went after browser passwords, crypto wallets, and Steam accounts.

Industry observers note that part of why these schemes work is that growing up online isn't the same as knowing how a computer works. Younger generations grew up on phones and apps that hide things like file permissions and security settings, so a warning on a desktop computer can be easy to dismiss. A 2023 Dell Technologies survey of more than 15,000 people ages 18 to 26 found that 44 percent were taught only very basic digital skills in school, and 12 percent got no digital skills education at all, according to Fortune.

In a recent development, apple Photos got a lot of newly introduced features in iOS 27, but the recent release of iOS 27.2 brought even more improvements. Here’s what’s new.

Shared Albums are among my favorite features in the Photos app. I don’t post on social media often, but I love using Shared Albums because they provide a social media-style experience in a private way that lives right inside Photos.

iOS 27 brought a variety of big improvements to Shared Albums. And in iOS 27.2, Apple introduced four more.

Per Apple’s release notes, here’s what’s newly introduced:.

To get these upcoming features, you’ll need to make sure your Shared Albums have been upgraded for iOS 27.

One complication introduced by AI is that it can be hard to know if an image is real or AI-generated.

This challenge extends to AI-edited photos too, which might have key details changed by tools like iOS 27’s Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up features in Photos.

Apple is tackling the glitch with its new Reference Image feature in iPhone 18 Pro, and also through a software enhancement that rolled out in iOS 27.2.

Per Apple, its latest software patch adds the following:.

Support for SynthID watermarking to help identify whether an image was generated or modified with generative tools in Photos and Image Playground.

Industry observers note that synthID is a cross-platform standard developed by Google that embeds unnoticeable digital watermarks into AI-modified photos. Users won’t see a visible watermark, but anyone who checks for a SynthID marker will find it.

Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone people when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four fresh features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now.

In a recent development, 9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The latest interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the fresh design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 was released to everyone last week. You can enhancement in the Settings app on your iPhone.

Apple and American Express recently revealed a upcoming partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

In a recent development, when shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a latest “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

Recent findings suggest that american Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a upcoming “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

It has been revealed that this feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:.

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

It has been revealed that iPhone people with select banks can manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

In a recent development, this one isn’t really a latest feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has declared that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.

As of November, Walmart’s roll out of Apple Pay across the United States is complete.

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

Anthropic is rolling out a upcoming Claude app for Android that picks up a Material 3 Expressive redesign.

Confirmed on Twitter/X by Anthropic Product Manager Robert Bye, Claude is now rolling out a Material 3 Expressive redesign for its Android app that, while not a full embrace of Google’s design language, does make a clear attempt to better fit in on Android.

Industry observers note that the updated design picks up a bottom-bar UI as opposed to relying fully on the old hamburger menu – it still exists, but it’s mainly for chat history now. You can see M3 elements throughout the app, including in the model switcher and the background of chats. It’s clearly themed to match Anthropic’s aesthetic, and there’s no obvious implementation of Material You colors, but it all fits within the general Material 3 guidelines – much more so than the original app.

The one flaw we spotted was the predictive back implementation, which gets a neat animation to move the search bar but is supposed to show a preview of the previous screen, but that’s just nit-picking, really.

The new Claude app for Android is rolling out now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun new trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.
  • The Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time.
  • Using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun new trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.

The Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time. For anyone who travels often or just has a lot of devices on hand, chargers like this are a must. Having something you don’t have to think twice about when it comes to charging rates is just so nice, and these have come a long way, too.

Using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide. I remember having single-port chargers that could barely fast-charge my phone that were twice this size just a few years ago. GaN just absolutely rules, and Baseus is using a special version that reduces heat and improves efficiency.

But the two reasons I really like this charger aren’t strictly to do with GaN.

The first is the built-in display. Again, that’s a trend throughout the industry. Anker has several chargers out with built-in displays as the company helped to really make this popular – the Anker Prime 160W brick is really similar to PicoGo Pro (at a higher price), and it’s the only I’ve been using for months before trying out this Baseus model.

According to recent reports, baseus has a cute little animated character that accompanies your charging, with little eyes when the charger isn’t active and some fun animations to show your charging rate in real-time. Neat! You can “press” the button to move through the UI and even see the specific charging rate of each connected device. You’ll also see that the brick can recognize the device you have plugged in, though Android devices just show a generic “SAMSUNG” or whatever brand you plug in – Anker, again, had a similar set of features in a brick released earlier in 2026, but some of those features were iPhone-only, and that brick was only a 1-port, 45W charger anyway.

But, like that Anker brick, Baseus supports “smart” charging that adjusts to your device. Plugging in a Galaxy Z Fold 8 that was around 65% full, I saw the brick adjust its charging speed to tailor to the phone, initially going up to full speed before settling down around 28W~. You can manually adjust this with “Turbo” or “Gentle” modes, the former maxing out the charging rate and the latter settling in around 15W for a slower charge. That flexibility is great because it means you can adjust the charging rate to what you need in that moment. Full-speed for a quick top-off on a busy day, slower charging overnight to preserve battery health.

Baseus isn’t doing much new here, though the GaN tech mentioned earlier is enhanced by some architecture and algorithm adjustments the company has made behind the scenes, but it’s a really good implementation.

Beyond that, it’s also priced pretty well.

In a recent development, baseus PicoGo Pro’s full price is $59.99, but you’ll probably rarely see it there. Technically, today is its launch date, and it’s already down by over 30% at $39.70 for Black Friday. Value-wise, this one is hard to beat.

As the story of a soccer team gone cannibal kicks off in 1996, Yellowjackets has plumbed the depths of '90s music to make one banger soundtrack season after season. Let's kick things off with the Season 4 premiere:.

Sample lyric: If I could find that Heina / And that Sancho that she's found / Well, I'd pop a cap in Sancho / And I'd slap her down.

Season 4 opens with this hit song that had a total chokehold on teens in 1996. The lyrics sing of a hapless dude making messy decisions.

Fittingly, it plays while teen Jeff (Jack DePew) is getting high on the job at Taylor's Furniture Store with his doofy bestie Randy (Riley Baron). Despite some violent lyrics, "Santeria" is a upbeat tune that speaks to Jeff's laid-back attitude, post-graduation.

But once he sees the news of the Yellowjackets rescue on TV, the theme song cuts in and dramatically changes the episode's tone.

Sample lyric: It was cool / Nothing fire / Nothing broke / Keep simple / Nothing tired / Nothing old / Same as you / Same as you.

For four seasons now, this song's cryptic lyrics have played as a pitch-perfect distillation of the show's female rage, rooted in lust, jealousy, and even love.

Sample lyric: My girl, my girl, don't lie to me / Tell me, where did you sleep last night?In the pines, in the pines / Where the sun don't ever shine / I would shiver the whole night through.

After the opening credits, Yellowjackets picks up with the titular team in a hospital, where they are safe but look worried, likely about the world learning how it is they made it through their ordeal.

Sources indicate that playing over the sequence is Kurt Cobain's cover of the American folk song also known as "In the Pines," which is recognized as a murder ballad. The lyrics reflect a haunting story of homicide in the woods. The particular song has been covered by a variety of acts since its creation in the 1870s, including the father of Bluegrass Bill Monroe, Blues singer Lead Belly, and Dolly Parton.

Cobain famously covered the song on his MTV Unplugged appearance, on Nov. 18, 1993. So, it's a cover the Yellowjackets themselves might recognize. Moreover, his grunge rendition reflects the trauma and terror of the team's return to civilization.

This '90s song plays in the present timeline, but in a meaningful way. Showing up to Shauna's (Melanie Lynskey) door in episode 1, Melissa (Hilary Swank) presents a bottle of wine along with the news that she's moved in next door, and that she's called the press. Shauna looks on in shock asking, "What did you do?" as "The Freshmen" plays.

From 1997, this hit song from the Verve Pipe tells the tale of two young men, reflecting on the damage they've done to a shared lover. In this context, "The Freshmen" plays as if Shauna's subconscious is making an excuse ("we were merely freshmen").

Or perhaps, this song's use use here is meant to reflect Melissa's perspective. As the wounded lover, her story could show what might happen if that lover struck back with the poetic justice of reclaiming her narrative and her future.

Sample lyric: Words like violence / Break the silence / Come crashing in / Into my little world / Painful to me / Pierce right through me / Can't you understand / Oh my little girl?

Needle drops are often non-diegetic, meaning the characters within the film or TV show don't hear them. But "Enjoy the Silence" is played within the world of Yellowjackets, while teen Shauna (Sophie Nélisse) is listening to the radio with her mom (Gabrielle Miller). Still covered in bruises from the beating she took at the hands of her teammates in the wilderness, she's subjected to the salt in the wound of the wider world's speculations.

Her mom clicks from one station to the next, and each one features someone squawking about the team, including two radio DJs who make crass jokes about the team "eating each other." In response, Shauna's mom switches off the radio, and states, "I feel like a little quiet." But the quiet is too much for Shauna, so she clicks the radio on, and "Enjoy the Silence" plays.

The Depeche Mode song from 1990 is a love song, so it's fitting that it plays as a photo of Jackie (Ella Purnell) swings from the vehicle's rear-view mirror. Even out of the wilderness, in silence or song, or her mother's car, Shauna can't escape her first true love. But even more haunting is the following lyric: "Words are very unnecessary / They can only do harm." In Yellowjackets, this song, which plays while Shauna returns to her house before a captive audience of newscasters, speaks to how silence is how the team can protect themselves from the civilized world.

Sample lyric: Thirty-eight chrome to the dome / It's on. You better be strapped when you're rolling in my zone.

Industry observers note that this hip-hop track plays when teen Shauna visits teen Jeff at the Woodbury Apartments, where he shares a place with Randy. The music begins as a non-diegetic tune, but then becomes part of the diegetic soundtrack of their bachelor pad, which also features a Tommy Boy poster and empty beer bottles.

It's a song that sets up the bro-hang environment that Shauna's crashing, which is reflected in how it stops as she enters the apartment. Sharp-eared Yellowjackets fans might remember this song also played in Season 2, episode 3 ("Digestif") when Jeff (Warren Kole) picked a fight at a gym with the late Kevyn Tan (Alex Wyndham).

Sample lyric: You're my angel, sticking on me / You're my angel, bringing me to my knees.

Recent findings suggest that this 1994 track from comes from the Los Angeles rock band that dog. In episode 2, it begins playing in the current timeline as Jeff approaches one of his billboards for Sadecki Furniture. It's been defaced by Shauna, who painted out letters so it reads "Sad Unit" next to Jeff's smiling face.

In a recent development, then, the song continues as the episode leaps back to the wilderness, where Natalie (Sophie Thatcher) brings blankets to the pit. There, the spikes and Mari's (Alexa Barajas) remains have been cleared away, and Lottie (Courtney Eaton) and Shauna are being held within so they can't harm others or themselves. The song ends as Shauna asks if the radio call to civilization worked. When Nat assures her it did, she begins to weep, then yells, "We're going to be so totally fucked!" As Nat walks away looking spooked, "Angel" kicks back in.

In both instances, the song is directly tied to Shauna, who is certainly an angel of vengeances, no matter how petty.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Translate is the latest first-party app to get a new icon, and it comes 11 years after the last redesign.

Google last updated the Translate icon in 2015. One thing to note is that the Android app uses a circular version that goes edge-to-edge.

Industry observers note that we’re seeing a newly introduced favicon on translate.google.com today. The old paper-esque background is gone, with Google removing the “physical” crease, but the inspiration is still there.

Sources indicate that muuuuuuuch nicer. Brings it up to date with the other newer icon designs.

The corners have been aggressively rounded, while the back layer with the Chinese character for language or writing is now light blue. Up front, the gradient is in full effect. The latest icon is a bit shorter than before.

This is a much more modern icon that fits nicely with the recent redesigns of Google’s communication and Workspace apps. On Android, it will presumably be placed on a white background.

This icon is not yet live on Android or iOS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, yellowjackets is back. With Season 4 comes newly introduced mysteries and new opening title cards inviting viewers to speculate on what's next. With each episode, Mashable will be probing these details, looking for questions and their answers. So, buckle up.

The theme song, "No Return" by Craig Wedren and Anna Waronker, roars to life over VHS footage once more. Some images are classic, like pre-crash footage of the team smiling and Jackie (Ella Purnell) smirking on the soccer pitch and drawing a threatening finger across her neck. But others are latest.

In Season 4, Episode 1, here are all the curious images we noticed:.

Recent findings suggest that melanie Lynskey is shown wide-mouthed before a microphone, suggesting adult Shauna has something to say (or sing?) in Season 4. Considering Shauna has a special skill for brutal one-liners, whoever she's looking at should be trembling.

In a recent development, under blood and a prosthetic broken nose, Sophie Nélisse is hard to recognize in the moment. But freeze-frame the credits, and there's no doubt that's Teen Shauna. She's lying in the snow. So, presumably this is still when the girls were in the wilderness.

In a recent development, at the end of the Season 3, Natalie (Sophie Thatcher) successfully reached the outside world through the frog scientist's SAT phone. So, what happens before rescue comes?

In episode 2, this mystery is solved. When Shauna rages about the revelation that Nat is calling for help, the others respond by throwing stones. Literally. The Antler Queen is violently dethroned as the team goes from chucking rocks at Shauna to descending on her in a flurry of punches and kicks. When Nat gets back to camp, she's shocked to see how the mighty have fallen, or more specifically, how beat to hell Shauna's face is.

The colors of this shot are brighter and more saturated than Yellowjackets tends to go. The uniform is a throwback 1950s style, and actress Tawny Cypress is smiling in a wide-eyed way that's not in keeping with Taissa's character. So, we're speculating this will be another dream sequence or vision. This one feel Lynchian, and as his work touches on doomed romances and the dark underbelly of suburbia, one can assume he'd speak to Taissa on both levels. But what does it mean?

Her face is covered by a mask, but there's no mistaking her frizzy blond hair and glasses. Will the girls' return to civilization show Misty's path to working at the old folks home? Or will this be a dream sequence where she imagines what her future might be?

In a recent development, in the credits, it's a close-up of what appears to be Shauna, wearing a blindfold and holding a string. To get a fuller context, you have to look to the sneak peek images Paramount released on Nov. 5. There you can see a wider shot:.

According to recent reports, here you can see she's holding a knife on a string while standing inside the crashed plane, her team huddled on the floor around her. This recalls the ritual seance the girls did in Season 1 in the cabin's attic. They'd tried to contact the presumed dead owner of the cabin, and instead tapped into something darker and more mysterious.

The swinging knife is meant to answer the girls' questions. So, are they calling on the "it" of the wilderness for advice ahead of their rescue?

Whose head is being pried open in this nightmarish way? It's hard to tell from the close-up, which gives away no facial features. Dark hair and a sleeve ending in lace are the only clues. But based on the outrageousness, we're going to guess this one is a nightmare within the show.

According to recent reports, this set dressing was spotted by fans on Reddit eight months back. But what's its role in the show? Well, we know Jackie's parents have money. Could this be how they memorialize their golden girl?

That's probably bad news for Shauna, right?

It has been revealed that christina Ricci's been a violent ax-wielder before. (We remember Lizzie Borden Took an Ax and The Lizzie Borden Chronicles). We also know an ax is how Edwin died last season — though by Lottie's hand. Yet despite Misty's maniacal facial expression, and her still wearing Natalie's leather jacket, we're guess this is more a Misty-to-the-rescue moment. Maybe she's about to pull a Shining and ax a door?

It has been revealed that where is she? WHO IS SHE AIMING AT?

As this is shot comes from the opening scene of Season 4, there's not much mystery here. Teen Jeff (Jack DePew) had moved on from Shauna and Jackie, getting high with Randy (Riley Baron) and working at Jackie's parents' furniture story. Then he sees her face on the news, with reports of their rescue.

With Shauna finally coming back from the wilderness, we're likely to see how grief and love brought these two together for a marriage we may not envy, but kind of admire?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You might have clocked it in the Season 4 premiere, but with episode 2 it's very clear: Molly Ringwald has joined Yellowjackets.
  • The '80s icon who fronted movies like The Breakfast Club, Sixteen Candles, and Pretty in Pink takes over the role of Van's (Liv Hewson) mom, Vicky Palmer, from Deborah Vancelette.
  • Recent findings suggest that in the Season 1 pilot, Vicky (Vancelette) is presented as a bad mom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You might have clocked it in the Season 4 premiere, but with episode 2 it's very clear: Molly Ringwald has joined Yellowjackets.

The '80s icon who fronted movies like The Breakfast Club, Sixteen Candles, and Pretty in Pink takes over the role of Van's (Liv Hewson) mom, Vicky Palmer, from Deborah Vancelette. And this signifies a major change in Van's life, post-rescue.

Recent findings suggest that in the Season 1 pilot, Vicky (Vancelette) is presented as a bad mom. In a montage of the Yellowjackets readying for that fateful flight, Van walks through a dark, cluttered house to find her mom passed out on the couch, next to a nearly empty alcohol bottle. She tries to wake her, presumably because she needs a ride to the plane. But calling to her and shaking her isn't enough to rouse Vicky. So, Van slaps her, and she does so with a world-weariness that suggests this isn't an isolated incident.

In Season 4, episode 2, Vicky (Ringwald) is transformed. The living room is sunny and tidy upon Van's return, with a wall of VHS tapes carefully preserved. Later, Vicky shows she cares by assuring Van she taped every episode of The X-Files. To Tai (Jasmin Savoy Brown), she'll say of Vicky, "My mom is completely different.".

No shade to Vancelette, who got little to do in the role of Vicky. But if any Yellowjacket was going to get a mom played by a movie idol of the '80s, it ought to be Van. Her love of pop culture is a defining characteristic, as she'd quote and allude to movies and highlights to brandish her wit and wisdom. Of course, if her mom's going to get a glow-up, she's going to become the "princess" from The Breakfast Club. Where other mothers wear furrowed brows before their recovered kids (or don't even show up, as is the case for poor Nat (Sophie Thatcher)), Van's mom is radiant with joy to bring her girl home for a fresh start. When Van picks up the home phone to listen for a dial tone, Vicky knows what's up, asking if she's checking to see the phone's connected in case someone calls. This shows that Van's mom knows she's up on her bills, and she knows her daughter.

More than that, Vicky gives Van the kind of heart-to-heart she's probably only ever seen in the movies before. "I know that I haven't been someone that you can count on. And that kills me," she confesses on the couch — this time sitting up, having put together a sprawling feast of snack foods for them to enjoy. "But this last year and a half has had a profound effect on me. And I think that it has for you too, and I would really love to understand how.".

But, first, a dentist appointment, because — much to Van's surprise — they have dental insurance now.

Deadline reported on the recasting back in February. Now, seeing Ringwald in action in the world of Yellowjackets, we can't wait to see what comes next.

  • One feature I haven’t found myself using (or noticing) very often is the heart rate sensor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it’s been just over a year since Apple released AirPods Pro 3, and I can confidently say I’ve worn them every day since. After a year of heavy use, I’m even more convinced that AirPods Pro 3 are the best money you can spend on Apple gear (especially at current sale pricing).

It has been revealed that while the changes to AirPods Pro 3 fit have been controversial to some users, I’ve been thoroughly impressed over the last year. I find them incredibly comfortable, and I absolutely notice the improvement in noise cancellation enabled by the updated in-ear fit. The sound quality, of course, is also excellent, and is made better by the updated shape.

One feature I haven’t found myself using (or noticing) very often is the heart rate sensor. This is probably because I always wear an Apple Watch. Apple notes that AirPods Pro 3 and Apple Watch can work together to get you the most accurate heart rate data possible. I assume this happens in the background, but I never notice or think about it.

An interesting twist to AirPods Pro 3 is that they actually have worse battery life on paper than AirPods Pro 2.

I haven’t noticed the overall lower battery life at all. On long travel days, however, I absolutely appreciate the longer battery life from the buds themselves. I can now comfortably wear them from my departure airport to my arrival airport on most travel days. And I don’t have any issues just placing my AirPods Pro 3 on a Qi charger on my desk to refuel.

One thing I love about AirPods is that they continuously get better with software updates. AirPods Pro 3 are no different. In addition to bug fixes and performance improvements, here are some of the upcoming features that have come to AirPods Pro 2 since they were released:.

Here’s what I wrote in my AirPods Pro 3 review last year:.

I often tell people that AirPods are the best bang-for-your-buck product in Apple’s lineup. They’re one of my most-used Apple products, and I’m sure I could do some math to prove they have the lowest cost-per-use of anything I own. AirPods Pro 3 are the best $249 you can spend with Apple today, and they feel like a turning point in what we should expect from the category going forward.

One year later, I stand by this paragraph. Also, note that I wrote $249 in that paragraph. Right now, AirPods Pro 3 are on sale for $149. That is an absolutely absurd value. If you’re on the fence, there’s never been a better time to join the AirPods Pro 3 club.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google Docs is getting an update in how it handles Microsoft Word documents, adding the ability to compare revisions without converting the file.
  • It has been revealed that you can already upload a Microsoft Word document (.docx) to Google Drive and use it within Docs without converting the file, but there are some limits.
  • In a recent development, rolling out now, Google Docs can now directly compare two documents, even if one is in a Microsoft Word format.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Docs is getting an update in how it handles Microsoft Word documents, adding the ability to compare revisions without converting the file.

It has been revealed that you can already upload a Microsoft Word document (.docx) to Google Drive and use it within Docs without converting the file, but there are some limits. One of those was comparing documents, which Google is now fixing with an upgrade.

In a recent development, rolling out now, Google Docs can now directly compare two documents, even if one is in a Microsoft Word format. To do this, you’ll need to upload the Word document to Drive, then select it in the “compare documents” tool, with Docs then showing any differences between the two. There are plenty of scenarios where this is useful, including when comparing versions of a contract.

This new feature is enabled for all users, and the company is apparently looking at similar functionality for PowerPoint files too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has a new “Priority Notifications” feature in the works for Pixel phones with the ability to pull your most important information to the top of the screen and even highlight it with a bit of color.

Google Pixel phones already have tools to manage your notifications, but an upcoming upgrade seems to be building on that functionality. The folks at Android Authority flipped the switch on some work-in-progress changes that reveal “Priority Notifications.”.

In a recent development, this is a newly introduced feature that Google describes as “highlighting urgrent messages” and “time-critical updates” by adding color to the notification and placing it at the top of the stock. Android’s notifications list already tries to place messages at the top, but it sounds like this AI-powered feature will further emphasize that. It’s also mentioned that this is powered by on-device AI.

Google’s early blurb describes:.

Highlight urgent messages, deliveries, and time-critical updates with hints of color at the top of your notifications.

Priority notifications use Al on your device, which may sometimes make mistakes. Your notifications are never sent to Google.

Recent findings suggest that the feature would also integrate with HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro series and the feature allows owners to exclude certain apps. Google also seems to be shuffling the branding, turning “Notification intelligence” into “Notification organizer,” and the existing organizer section into “Notification bundles.”.

Exactly when this might land on Pixel phones is unknown. It’s not mentioned what build this feature was found hiding in, but it seems likely it was in the ongoing QPR3 beta. QPR3’s stable release will arrive around March 2027, but there’s no guarentee it’ll bring this new feature with it.

💡 Key Takeaways

She had been developing a crew-led version of the podcast since her estranged husband and co-host, Ethan Klein, was pushed out of it last month after she revealed his affair.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I've come to realize that I can't continue down this path while also giving myself the space I need to heal and protect my mental health," she wrote.
  • The announcement closes out a month-long fallout that began on Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The H3 Podcast has come to an end.

On Monday, Hila Klein confirmed on the show's Instagram account that she had "made the difficult decision to stop working on the new show." She had been developing a crew-led version of the podcast since her estranged husband and co-host, Ethan Klein, was pushed out of it last month after she revealed his affair.

Recent findings suggest that "I've come to realize that I can't continue down this path while also giving myself the space I need to heal and protect my mental health," she wrote. "Right now, I need to focus on myself, my healing, and what's best for me and my kids.".

The announcement closes out a month-long fallout that began on Oct. 22. That day, Ethan stated on Instagram Stories that the podcast was going on "indefinite hiatus." Hours later, Hila posted that he had been having an affair for more than six months. As Mashable previously reported, the crew said in a statement that they would not keep working with Ethan "involved or profiting in any way." Ethan said he was working to give up his financial stakes in the podcast and in the couple's businesses, including the clothing brand Teddy Fresh.

Sources indicate that complex reported that Hila filed for divorce on Nov. 2, listing their separation date as Oct. 13. The couple married in 2012 and share three children.

Since the news broke, multiple crew members have spoken out. On the show's Discord, longtime producer GirlWithAMicrophone (GWAM) remarked she would not work on a project with the rest of the crew. She thanked Hila for giving them "a shot during all this turmoil.".

Producer AB Ayad suggested on X that the obstacles were bigger than any one person. "There are certain people involved that were never gonna allow us to continue doing the show together," he wrote, adding, "I give Hila a lot of credit that she was able to do what she even did.".

Beyond the H3 Podcast, Ethan co-hosted Frenemies with Trisha Paytas, which became one of YouTube's most talked-about shows before it ended acrimoniously in 2021. He later started the political show Leftovers with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, which ended in 2023 over disagreements about Israel and the war in Gaza.

Recent findings suggest that since the announcement of the show ending, Ethan has broken his weeks-long silence. On Tuesday, in a series of Instagram Stories, he called the affair "the ultimate betrayal" to his wife and to the show's audience. He also remarked that "the show ending is entirely my fault.".

However, he didn't rule out a comeback. "I will probably be back, but when and how, I can't tell you," he wrote, hinting at a solo show or a new project.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that apple has introduced several exciting new products in the last month, including iPhone Duo and the redesigned MacBook Pro.
  • Two years ago when Mark Gurman published an in-depth report on Apple’s forthcoming HomeView, I was immediately ready to buy one.
  • After numerous delays, the HomeView is finally here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple has introduced several exciting new products in the last month, including iPhone Duo and the redesigned MacBook Pro. But my personal favorite new product is Apple’s HomeView. Here’s how I’ve been using it.

Two years ago when Mark Gurman published an in-depth report on Apple’s forthcoming HomeView, I was immediately ready to buy one.

After numerous delays, the HomeView is finally here. And despite several shortcomings I expect will be fixed with software updates, the HomeView overall is exactly what I’ve been wanting in a home product.

HomeView is essentially a HomePod, but with a screen. And that screen adds so much extra value.

When rumors said the HomeView would only have a 7-inch display, I was concerned it would be too small. It turns out, Apple knew what it was doing. The HomeView’s size is a feature, not a bug. Too much larger and it would stand out as a piece of tech. By staying small, the HomeView can be a cute, non-distracting addition to the home.

Here are some HomeView features I’ve been loving so far:.

According to recent reports, none of these is what I’d call a “killer feature,” but together they amount to a delightful experience. I already liked having a HomePod around, and HomeView builds on that foundation in so many ways.

Overall, HomeView is very much the product I was hoping for back in 2024. That mentioned, there’s definitely room for improvement. Here’s what’s missing.

Industry observers note that I love HomeView for what it is today, but I fully expect Apple to improve the product via software updates. Leaks already point to two major feature upgrades in the works that I hope ship soon.

Built-in apps for Apple Photos and Notes would be great to have, plus support for the recipes included in Apple News+. But my personal top request is for parental controls of some sort.

I completely agree, this is exactly the device I’ve been waiting for.

My only con… Siri AI is just slightly more than half-baked when it comes to voice prompts. One example, when we ask it for the weather forecast it gives us a one-line “It’s going to rain today.” That’s not a forecast. 🙃 So we’re forced to follow up with “more details please”. When we do… 🙂 … we get an actual forecast. Asking it for a recap of today’s headlines is hit or miss too. These are just two of a handful of examples where Siri AI is only about 60% of what Alexa+ is for conversational AI purposes.

According to recent reports, with that one nod to the nut jobs out there claiming an old iPad suffices everyone on planet earth perfectly well, I’m still giddy about the fact that I can browse through my full library of music on Apple Music, Amazon Music, and iBroadcast and try upcoming “suggested” albums/playlists without having to have my iPhone with me everywhere I go in the house. While I spent $299 mainly for an enhanced music experience, having it is priceless.

For a device that’s intended for the whole family, I’ve been surprised to find there are no current features to prevent young children from doing whatever they want with HomeView. I have a toddler who loves the HomeView so much that I had to move it out of his reach. I wish there was a way to lock the screen on command, or prevent switching apps or faces without authentication. Some sort of “toddler mode” would be greatly appreciated.

Siri AI has also had some bugs, but those are likely related to me running the iOS 27.3 beta.

Apple’s new HomeView is available now for $299.

What’s your take on the HomeView so far? Are you still mulling a purchase? Let us know in the comments.

After 12 years of awkward silences, flirting, and fried chicken, Chicken Shop Date is officially closed.

Sources indicate that the final episode of Amelia Dimoldenberg's YouTube series is now live, and for her last date, she sat down with Belgian psychotherapist Esther Perel. Dimoldenberg, called by the BBC "one of the U.K.'s best-known content creators," announced in September that the show was ending.

The show's final guest, Perel, is best known for her work on relationships and intimacy. So, given who's sitting across from her this episode, it's no surprise the conversation turns on Dimoldenberg and what it means to walk away from the show that made her.

"I can't stay here forever," Dimoldenberg says in tears near the end of the episode. "I need to leave the shop.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like clockwork, the first quarter of the Pixel 11 brings discounts, and this shines a light on the base model that needs to be explored.
  • By this point, you don’t need me to tell you that this is a familiar design.
  • I hoped that the maximum brightness bug would have been resolved by now with the screen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like clockwork, the first quarter of the Pixel 11 brings discounts, and this shines a light on the base model that needs to be explored.

By this point, you don’t need me to tell you that this is a familiar design. It’s turning into a comfortable pair of slippers at this point in time. Nothing is wrong, and nothing particularly stands out. A safe but samey design that is inoffensive.

I hoped that the maximum brightness bug would have been resolved by now with the screen. It creates a shadow around the edges of the display after a minute or so when in direct sunlight. Somewhat like blooming on a cheap LCD screen. It does diminish what is otherwise a great display.

The thickness has started to feel like a relic of the 2023 design that feels a little dated now. I have been using the Pixel 11 without a case most of the time, which mitigates it, but throw a case on and it’s a chunky boi. The added thickness would probably have been acceptable had the extra space been filled with more battery, but it feels like that boat has set sail a long time ago. A slimmer profile probably would have helped differentiate without deviating too much from last year’s phone.

After months of using the Pixel 11, the move of the NFC module to the top edge has been huge for me because my car uses an NFC terminal to lock and unlock when you’re without a set of car keys. With the Pixel 10, it worked but not quite as smoothly. It’s one of those inconsequential changes that makes a real-world difference.

Gemini Intelligence has been something I’ve started to rely on quite heavily. I love that I get a prompt to add an appointment to my calendar, and all of the crucial details have been taken care of, like the location, extra contact details, the works.

I’m not sure what the hold-up is for adding wider functionality. It’s actively hurting things, in my opinion. Google Messages is great, but some of the automation functions locked in there mean I haven’t been saving any time with Gemini’s prowess at doing the legwork of keeping my life up to date.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve tried using Pause Point, but found it’s just easier to leave my phone face down rather than use an app to try and stop using my phone…maybe if we all did that, so many of the world’s ills wouldn’t be so pronounced. Just a thought.

Sources indicate that the November Pixel Drop has also made some notable changes to the Pixel 11 experience that I can’t believe were held back since launch. If you waited and bought in the last few weeks with the substantial discounts kicking around, you objectively get a better phone today than at launch.

The improvements don’t overhaul things, just enhance or heighten the fluidity and experience above what was available in the months post-launch. More cohesive theming, little tweaks to the UI; it’s not reinventing the Pixel 11, just augmenting it in ways that would have been nice back in August.

Sources indicate that I don’t really have much to complain about with the Pixel 11 lifespan even after months of charging. Yes, charging is still slow, but you only need to charge once per day. If we were talking about a phone with bad battery life and slow charging, I’d have more to complain about. However, it’s still solid and dependable.

The camera continues to impress without really improving drastically. I can’t help but feel that every couple of generations, the Pro camera setup should be passed on to the base Pixel, then we get a newer, improved system on that specific Pro model. It’d allow for quicker improvements and maybe, dare I say it, make the camera system cheaper as parts get reused. If anything, it would help Google’s supposed environmental pledges by preventing camera components from hitting landfill.

In a recent development, A lot of people will tell you the best camera is the one you have with you, and this hasn’t ever been a problem for a recent Pixel. I can count on one hand the frustrations I have felt with the Pixel 11 camera since it landed on my desk on launch day. I am happier than a year ago with the base Pixel 10 than the 11, which is to say this is a bigger leap or a return to form.

In a recent development, having the ability to tune Camera Looks was something I have loved, but you might just fall into using one tuned look that fits your own personal style. There is an element of this that might change the perception of the Pixel 11 camera consistency versus its predecessors. What I mean is that while it does still excel at point-and-shoot, the fact that Looks are baked into the JPEG could be a problem. There are times when I’ve thought that an image might have been better using default settings.

That stated, I have stuck to “Shadows” with Contrast set to -5, Highlights to -5, Shadows to -5.5, warmth to 0.5, and Grain to “Strong.” That is a recipe I’ll probably stick with for a long time to come. It’s still weird that we can do all this at the camera level with a Pixel. Whether “normies” even use the options or just stick to the out-of-the-box default settings is another discussion for another day.

At $699, the Pixel 11 becomes a decent buy for a lot of people. For others, the distinct lack of power is something that can’t ever be overcome. I would buy this for a relative because it’ll do everything they could ever want and more. For a friend who cares about having the cutting edge in their pocket? Probably not.

A lot of the problems over the past few years on Pixel phones have come from the price tag.

Even with the discounts in and around Black Friday, the fact that you can get a device like the Galaxy S25 Ultra that’ll have better specs and lots of valuable features for around the same price. The last few generations of the Pixel have been harder to recommend because of the drawbacks versus the cost and the competition.

Industry observers note that I remarked a few months ago that there is a good phone under the price hikes, and that remains unchanged. However, there are better products from the year prior that won’t compromise and are even cheaper. In a silo, you’re getting a 7/10 product at a 3/10 price. Just how that changes depends on forthcoming updates. One saving grace is that no Pixel is ever quite the same months after it rolls off the production line. A few Pixel Drops, even more discounts, and maybe a true seal of approval might be easier.

To put it into context, this was never a $900 phone and arguably never should have been. That’s somewhat a failing on Google’s part in more ways than one. At least it’s down to a palatable price that should be the Pixel baseline.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that macOS 27.3 is launching next month alongside iOS 27.3 and more, and it includes a variety of latest features for Mac consumers.
  • macOS already supports running Live Activities from your iPhone via iPhone Mirroring.
  • The feature first debuted on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, which features Live Activities in the latest Dynamic Island.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that macOS 27.3 is launching next month alongside iOS 27.3 and more, and it includes a variety of latest features for Mac consumers. Here are three macOS 27.3 features coming soon.

macOS already supports running Live Activities from your iPhone via iPhone Mirroring. But in macOS 27.3, Apple is adding native support for Live Activities from Mac apps.

The feature first debuted on the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display, which features Live Activities in the latest Dynamic Island. But with macOS 27.3, the new feature expands to all Mac models and in a slightly different way.

Recent findings suggest that live Activities on Macs without a Dynamic Island will display in the menu bar. From there you can click to view full details, as seen above.

Safari introduces several upgrades across macOS 27.3, iOS 27.3, and iPadOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that vertical Tabs are one tentpole addition, providing a new option for how to view your tabs in Apple’s browser. When enabled, your tabs move from the top of the browser to the left side in a new column view.

Adaptive Dark Mode is another newly introduced feature. It automatically enables dark mode on many websites that don’t natively support it already. Finally, Siri AI gains support for new Safari actions, including the ability to interact with a full webpage using onscreen awareness, not just the parts that are right now visible.

Do you use Markdown, the popular John Gruber-created plain text syntax? If so, macOS 27.3 has a welcome addition: support for rendering Markdown in Quick Look.

Rather than needing to open Markdown files in apps to preview formatted text, macOS now lets you just use Quick Look and see all of your Markdown syntax rendered properly with links, headings, bold, italics, and more.

You can learn more about Markdown here on John Gruber’s site, Daring Fireball.

Which macOS 27.3 additions are you most interested in? Let us know in the comments.
