5 ways to make sure your console isn't holding back your GTA 6 performance

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 already pushes every PS5 and Xbox to its limit, but is yours falling short of it?
  • Within days of GTA 6's November 19 debut, Xbox owners had found a way to break its 30 fps cap.
  • It's fundamentally the processor that's holding GTA 6 at 30 fps on current-gen consoles (PS5 Pro included).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 already pushes every PS5 and Xbox to its limit, but is yours falling short of it?

Within days of GTA 6's November 19 debut, Xbox owners had found a way to break its 30 fps cap. The trick, which was first reported on November 22, involves flipping a Series X's output between 60Hz and 120Hz, then hopping in and out of the game using Quick Resume. It works... sort of. When Digital Foundry tested the trick, it found the uncapped Series X averaged about 36 fps over an hour of play. The game's cars and animations also moved noticeably faster than they're meant to (some at around double speed).

It's fundamentally the processor that's holding GTA 6 at 30 fps on current-gen consoles (PS5 Pro included). The fact that a Series X with the limiter switched off is only able to find six extra frames per second illustrates how little is left to play with, so tinkering with settings isn't going to do very much. What you can do, however, is check whether your console is making the most of its available hardware.

A system that's out of date, stuck in a stale session, choked with dust or reading the game off the wrong drive could easily fall short. Here's how to find out if yours is falling victim to any of these problems.

I've played around 60 hours of GTA 6 in the last week on an original-model PS5 I bought in 2021, and haven't seen too much dipping below 30 fps outside of full-on rampages. There are some drops, though, which aligns with others' findings that it regularly falls slightly under 30 fps during ordinary city drives, and dropped to 23 fps during a grenade launcher test with multiple explosions. The PS5 Pro fares much better, with stress tests finding that it maintains 30 fps for the most part, only dropping to around 24 fps when the player wrecks as many cars as possible all at once.

The Series X, meanwhile, generally holds its 30 fps target but can slip during busy scenes and explosions. The Series S, which renders at 720p internally, struggles quite a bit. It hovers between 25 and 30 fps for most of the game and drops to as low as 20 in busy areas and when vehicles start blowing up, with one explosive scene briefly tanking it to 18 or 19 fps during Kotaku's testing.

Since consoles don't have built-in frame rate counters, the simplest way to monitor fps is to watch for stuttering. If the action gets choppy during firefights, police chases, explosions and pile-ups, your frame rate is dropping, which is somewhat normal for current-gen console hardware. You shouldn't be losing frames during cutscenes or when walking or driving around normally, even on a Series S.

If you are, that's a sign something else is amiss with your console. As for native 40 or 60 fps modes, Rockstar's technology production director Marc Chambers has said that even the PS5 Pro's processor isn't powerful enough, settling a major question about GTA 6's controversial FPS decision.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar released GTA 6's first post-launch upgrade on November 23. The patch notes describe fixes for several issues that caused the game to crash, along with bugs that could stall playthroughs, from broken autosaves to story phone calls that wouldn't come through. Nowhere in the patch notes is frame rate or performance mentioned, though. The rumor mill started spinning up shortly after, claiming that Rockstar would push a stuttering fix on November 25, but nothing came of it.

To check whether your game is up to date on PS5, highlight GTA 6 on the main menu, press the Options button on your controller and select Check for Update. Xbox players should go to My games & apps, choose Manage and then check under Updates to see titles that have newer versions available. Storage might be an issue, given the base game's absolutely massive 212GB size. Sony has warned that installing data can require roughly twice as much free space as the install size, so a console that's filled to the brim might refuse to install the patch.

Sources indicate that players were still posting about error CE-108255-1 and others as recently as November 25. Sony describes it, rather vaguely, as an error with a game or application. If it keeps happening after updating, Sony's crash troubleshooting runs through installing the latest system software, starting a new save and, as a last resort, deleting and reinstalling the game.

Sources indicate that quick Resume on the Xbox Series X and S saves the state of a game when you switch to another one, then reloads that state when you come back. It's the feature that enables the frame rate glitch mentioned earlier. It works by setting the console to 60Hz, starting GTA 6, switching to 120Hz on the loading screen, launching a different game and then jumping back in through Quick Resume. This relaunches the game with its cap removed, allowing it to run faster than it's meant to — though it can lead to crashes and bugs.

In testing by Digital Foundry, the uncapped Series X only reached 60 fps when flying a plane with nothing but sky in view. It managed around 40 fps on highways with light traffic, but barely beat 30 in heavier scenes, such as busy streets. It concluded that 60 fps is simply out of reach on current hardware and that although a 40 fps mode with VRR could make sense on Series X, it wouldn't be a clear improvement over the current 30 fps cap.

Recent findings suggest that to get a clean start on Xbox, press the Xbox button, highlight GTA 6, press the Menu button and then select Quit. You can also manually choose which games use Quick Resume through Manage game and add-ons > Quick Resume settings on a game's tile. Microsoft added that feature back in April because Quick Resume doesn't always behave as intended in certain titles (particularly after a game has been inactive for a while).

The PS5, meanwhile, keeps games suspended in rest mode. Thus, closing GTA 6 by highlighting its icon on the main menu, pressing Options and choosing Close Game, or turning the console off completely, achieves the same result. Be sure to save your game regularly since you won't have sleep mode as a fallback.

In a recent development, sony's PS5 safety guide recommends keeping your console roughly 4 inches away from walls, out of closed cabinets or other cramped spaces, and off long-pile carpets. It should also be free of dust on its vents. Microsoft recommends similar for the Xbox: a well-ventilated, relatively cool spot away from heat sources, with nothing sitting on, under or right next to the console. Since both went on sale in late 2020, plenty of consoles have had six years to suck up dust.

It has been revealed that while neither Sony nor Microsoft notes that a hot console will lead to slower gameplay, heat stress wears components down more quickly. Also, if your PS5 gets too hot, you'll be met with an on-screen warning, at which point Sony recommends switching it off and letting it cool down to prevent damage. On Xbox, meanwhile, poor ventilation and/or overheating is one of two causes Microsoft gives for the console switching itself off without warning. So while a hot console won't necessarily cut the frame rate, it could crash your game or force your console to shut down.

There's also been speculation that overheating could be behind some of the PS5 crashes we've seen since GTA 6's launch. That's possibly because of degradation of the liquid metal that sits between the processor and its cooler. A clean console isn't a workaround for hardware limitations and faults, but it does remove heat as a potential suspect.

Sony says that before cleaning your PS5, you should unplug it and wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth. Its side covers come off, allowing you to clean the dust catchers more easily.

GTA 6 needs up to 212GB of free space on both consoles, which is close to a third of the roughly 667GB that's usable on an 825GB PS5. That might push you toward installing the game on a secondary M.2 SSD added to the console's expansion slot. While the PS5 is compatible with a wide range of PCIe Gen4 drives, Sony recommends a sequential read speed of 5,500 MB/s or faster and requires a heatsink or similar cooling. But even with a compatible drive faster than that, games won't necessarily perform the same as they would on the internal SSD.

It has been revealed that as you'd expect from such a dense title, the game is constantly pulling in data as you move around Leonida. Digital Foundry's Series S testing found frame rate drops in situations that put a heavy load on the console's AI or streaming, so the game leans on its storage more than others do.

According to recent reports, while we haven't seen any examples of GTA 6 behaving problematically when installed on an M.2 drive, if you're doing so and experience stutter when you shouldn't, moving the game back to internal storage is worth a try. On your PS5, go to Settings > Storage > M.2 SSD Storage > Move Games and Apps to move as needed. On an Xbox, Series X and S games can only run from the internal SSD or Microsoft's Storage Expansion Card, which Microsoft claims performs identically to the internal drive.

If you’re buying a robot vacuum, it should be self-emptying. It just wouldn’t make sense to buy one without that feature, given that the whole point is to make vacuuming as hands-off as possible.

I have two beagles, and I vacuum twice a day. That’s why I have what I like to call my Dreame Team: the Dreame L60 Pro Ultra, the Aero Pro Steam, and the N20 Steam Portable Carpet Cleaner. I also have a lone Shark upright. Clearly, I have enough cleaning to do without emptying a robot’s dustbin, too.

Luckily, almost every robot vacuum at Amazon seems to be on sale for Black Friday, and Mashable has tested so many robot vacuums. But when everything has a flashing red "Black Friday deal" label, figuring out which deals are genuinely good takes a little more work. That’s what Mashable's shopping team is here for.

Throughout Black Friday, I’ll be double-checking MSRPs, comparing prices across retailers, and watching for new deals from our favorite robot vacuum brands. As always, Mashable is here to get you the best value for your money this holiday season. So, without further ado, here are our picks for the best Black Friday self-emptying robot vacuum deals.

In a recent development, the Roborock Q10 S5+ is a Mashable fave. Not only is it an affordable option, but Leah Stodart, our former vacuum expert, found it reliably performed in her cleaning tests, including wiping up a variety of spills and splatters in her kitchen.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also super quiet, even when emptying its dustbin. Stodart liked its accurate mapping and sonic mopping, which actually scrubs rather than just dragging a damp pad across your floors. At $229.99, you’re getting more than a basic robot that picks up crumbs and calls it a day.

It has been revealed that the only downside? You'll have to wash the mop pad yourself, and Stodart noted that it gets dirty quickly. It also isn’t the most thorough around edges. But if you want a self-emptying robot vacuum without spending $500 or more, this is a good entry-level pick. Recent findings suggest that there's a current trend for deception games, partly driven by the popularity of TV's The Traitors. Chameleon sees a group of players take turn to describe a word or concept without actually saying it. But one player is actually the Chameleon and has to guess the word from the other players' clues — all while avoiding detection. It's a ridiculous amount of fun, and perfect for massive groups and players of all ages.

Catan is a veritable board game classic, and it's a great pick to snag while it's discounted. Three to four players settle a randomly laid-out island, collecting wood, brick, wool, grain, and ore to build roads, settlements, and cities. Games wrap up in about an hour to 90 minutes, and it's fairly easy to learn. And if you're tired of playing the same things over and over, Catan's modular board means no two games set up the same way. It's a significant upgrade from Monopoly that's suitable for the whole family.

Sources indicate that the classics are classic for a reason. Mouse Trap has delighted kids and families for years, and nothing has changed after all this time. Indeed, it's as fiddly to set up as it ever was, but there's no denying the fun of setting the trap in motion. Kids will love the mechanics, parents will love the nostalgia. You can also find Black Friday discounts on other kids classics, including Connect 4, Battleship, and Candy Land.

Sources indicate that if you've ever wanted to get started with Dungeons & Dragons but didn't know how, this board game is the perfect introduction. It has a quick-start guide, player boards for the Cleric, Rogue, Wizard, and Fighter, and cards for species, backgrounds, spells, and gear so nobody has to build a character from scratch. Three to five players run through three adventure booklets split between combat, exploration, and roleplaying, and the poster maps for the Keep and the Caves of Chaos pull from one of the oldest modules in the game’s history. It's got everything beginners need and then some, so it's a much less daunting introductory experience.

If you haven't played the Horrified series, it's worth checking out for team-based beast-slaying. Players join forces to take on various classic monster — in this version it's American monsters that include Bigfoot, the Jersey Devil, and Mothman — with different ways of killing each monster. Board game fans will be familiar with the mechanics of the gameplay but the great thing about it is that you can mix and match the monsters, so each time you play is different. It can also get pretty tense as you ratchet up the difficulty level.

Braun indicates a full-body session takes just 10 minutes (twice a month for three months), and a built-in skin tone sensor adjusts every flash automatically so you do not need protective glasses.

Black Friday week is finally here, and fittingly, so are some of the best Nintendo Switch 2 deals of the year.

The Switch is a console that's hard to catch on sale, especially following its $50 price hike in September. It's also one of the hottest Christmas gifts you can grab, and a Mashable Gift of the Year winner. That's why we were thrilled to see the $30 markdown on the console earlier this month. And right now, we're even more thrilled to see the Nintendo Switch 2 and Mario Kart bundle go live.

According to recent reports, considering one Switch 2 deal is a rarity, two is truly a holiday miracle. You'll want to act fast, though — the regular console deal is on sale through Dec. 5 or while supplies last, while the bundle deal is only live through Dec. 5.

According to recent reports, if you already own the console, you'll still want to check out our list below. Nintendo storage cards, games, and other accessories are also on sale for Black Friday. While stock is tight on the new Zelda version of the Switch 2, you can snag the standard model already on sale before Black Friday. Head to Woot to get the Nintendo Switch 2 while it's in stock for $469. Amazon Prime members get free shipping with Woot, but keep in mind that Woot deals tend to sell out rapidly, so don't wait on this one.

Industry observers note that mario fans, why not pick up a free game alongside your newly introduced Switch 2? At full price, the Switch 2 and Mario Kart bundle runs for $549.99. If you buy the console ($499.99) and game ($79.99) separately, the total will already read $579.98. Add in the $7.99 three-month Nintendo Switch Online individual membership included in the bundle, and you're at $587.97. In other words, the bundle at full price will save you $37.98. For its Black Friday price? You'll save a whopping $88.97.

This bundle is on sale at several retailers, but you'll get the absolute best deal at Amazon and Walmart, where it's down to $499. At Target, Best Buy, and Nintendo, the bundle is just slightly more at $499.99. According to Nintendo's website, this promotion will be live through Dec. 5.

Load up on all the games before winter break with a memory upgrade from the SanDisk 512GB microSD Express Card. It's designed with write speeds up to 650 MB/s and read speeds up to 880 MB/s. The SanDisk microSD is officially licensed by Nintendo for the Switch 2, so you'll be good to go for all your gaming needs. With memory in short supply and prices rising, snag this deal before it expires.

According to recent reports, black Friday has always been the best time to buy a laptop, and that's still holding true in 2026 despite RAMageddon. While the holiday season's top discounts on MacBooks and Windows PCs may not look as great as usual due to industry-wide price hikes, they're still shaping up to be retailers' most competitive offers of the year.

Sources indicate that in fact, some of the latest Black Friday laptop deals are even better than I expected. (I monitor laptop prices year-round for Mashable.) MacBook Air deals maxed out at $250 last year, but right now, some configurations are up to $300 off. And the MacBook Neo is finally seeing its first proper price cut for non-students.

On the PC side, I'm impressed by the number of budget Windows laptops that are currently on sale for $700 or less, and by the number of gaming laptops that are close to $1,000 off. For those with deeper pockets, note that some of this fall's latest Nvidia RTX Spark laptops are on sale for the first time ever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday is finally here, and that means deals on PlayStation games, accessories, and more are live at Amazon and plenty of other major retailers. With the debut of Grand Theft Auto VI and a slew of other great titles available right now, it's a good time to pick up a spare controller, a headset, or a few titles you've been waiting on.

Shopping now also puts you ahead of the holiday rush, with a better shot at finding what you want in stock and getting it delivered in time for gift giving. Many of these prices are set to last through the weekend and into Cyber Monday, though popular items can sell out before then, especially with the demand for accessories and consoles in general to play the biggest game release of the year (and potentially all time.).

It has been revealed that if you’re shopping for a PS5 console, you're going to run into a bit more difficulty when it comes to availability and sales. We haven't seen any deals worth mentioning just yet, but we're keeping an eye out.

It has been revealed that if you're looking to buy a PS5 this year, you'll be hard-pressed to find one. Grand Theft Auto VI just arrived on Nov. 19, and PS5 demand has spiked ever since. Sony calls the game the biggest launch in PlayStation history and indicates more latest PS5 consoles came online in one day than ever before. It’s a one-month subscription to Peak, the tech giant’s mid-tier initiative that includes core features such as readiness scores and advanced features like health and stress monitoring. The Whoop free trial includes a pre-owned Whoop 5.0 device and wired charger, along with a brand-new band of your choice. According to Whoop, the pre-owned device is thoroughly tested to ensure it works, but it may have minor cosmetic flaws.

In a recent development, once the trial ends, your membership will automatically renew at $239 per year unless canceled beforehand. If you decide to cancel, you’ll need to return your device and battery pack, and you’ll be responsible for the cost of shipping ($6).

Recent findings suggest that whoop’s annual memberships are not cheap. Fortunately, Whoop’s referral program lets you earn free months to offset future membership fees. For each friend you refer, you receive one month of membership credit, and your friend receives one free month upon joining. If you have a month-to-month blueprint, referral credits apply to the next monthly charge until fully used. If you have a 12- or 24-month prepaid plan, credits will extend your renewal date. Referral credits are applied only after your friend has passed their return window or made their second payment, whichever comes first.

Active and retired military members, as well as first responders, are eligible for a 10 percent Whoop discount on the Peak ($239/year) and Life ($359/year) memberships. You must verify your status via ID.me to receive the Whoop promo code.

According to recent reports, like the discount above, students can save 10% on Whoop. This 10% Whoop student discount applies to Peak, Life, and One memberships. To get the Whoop promo code for 10% off, simply verify your student status through StudentBeans.

According to recent reports, say what you will about gift cards, but in the world of biohacking, a Whoop gift card is practically a love language. Instead of buying a Whoop device outright, which requires choosing both the membership and the band, a gift card is a thoughtful alternative. Gift cards are available in $25, $50, $75, $100, $250, or $1,000 amounts. Gift card numbers are delivered by email with instructions for redeeming them at checkout. You can either choose a specific recipient or send it to yourself to print and give in person. Please note that gift cards cannot be returned or exchanged, so I recommend this only if you know your friend has been dying for a Whoop.

In a recent development, whoop offers a Whoop Family Plan to help everyone reach their goals more affordably. You’ll also get a lifetime warranty and 24/7 support. The Whoop Family Plan is for two to six people, and instead of each member paying an individual membership fee, the family has a single annual bill. Be sure to check out Whoop Family Memberships to see if it’s right for your clan.

Whoop wants to make taking charge of your health easier than ever with Whoop Advanced Labs.

On non-fertile days, it’ll give you a green status, and on days when you could get pregnant without protection, it’ll show a red status. And if you’re already a Natural Cycles member, you can get 50% off Whoop annual Peak or Life memberships.

When it comes to hair gadgets, there are many gimmicks that claim to make styling easy and effortless, but the Dyson Airwrap actually works, using air to draw strands of your hair around the curling barrels to produce a lasting result without subjecting your hair to excessive damaging heat. It's a multifunction styler, but the Airwrap really shines as a curling iron. Powered by its internal motor, it creates a vortex of air inside the hollow barrel, powerful enough to draw your hair to it. All you have to do is place the end of your hair near the barrel, and the machine does the gripping and wrapping for you, so you don't have to worry about touching a hot curling barrel.

It has been revealed that nike has been having a bit of a comeback—“comeback” might be generous, but the sentiment is there. In 2024, the sportswear giant faced restructuring challenges, accusations of sexism, and layoffs that exceeded two percent of its staff. After difficult years marked by falling sales, poor innovation, and strained retail partnerships, CEO John Donahoe resigned, and organization veteran Elliott Hill returned in his place. Under Hill’s leadership, Nike is refocusing on its core market and working to repair relationships with retailers, athletes, and creatives.

Industry observers note that despite these shortcomings, Nike remains one of the most popular brands worldwide. Having worked at a Nike outlet for a year, I can tell you that unless you need something immediately, paying full price is rarely worthwhile. Most Nike products eventually go on sale through seasonal discounts or promotions. In the meantime, I’ve rounded up some of the current best Nike coupons and promo codes to help you save.

Sources indicate that ready to up your shoe game this winter? Level up for less with the Nike Black Friday 2026 Deals. During the sale, enjoy 15 to 40% off apparel and shoes for women, men, and children. Whether you want a fresh pair of Nike Air Force 1 Low Retros or a Big Kids' Long-Sleeve T-Shirt for your kiddo, there’s something on sale for everyone.

Industry observers note that remember earlier when I mentioned Nike members get rewarded? Be sure to become a Nike member before your birthday month to receive a special birthday discount. Not only will you get that birthday perk, but as a Nike member you’ll also get free shipping on orders of $50 or more, a free 60-day Wear Test to ensure the purchase is right for you, and returns with receipts.

It has been revealed that all students over 16 in the US, whether you’re in high school, college, or a university, get 10% off at Nike, Nike.com, and in the Nike app. To get the Nike discount code, you’ll need to verify your student status. To do this, you’ll need to fill out a verification form, confirm your age, and you may need to provide documentation to verify your status. Once your status is successfully verified, you’ll receive a single-use Nike promo code for 10% off most items. You’ll need to make sure you're signed in to your Nike Member profile while using your Nike promo code. This 10% Nike discount code can be used on a wide range of Nike apparel and shoes, including the bestselling Nike Vomero Plus men’s running shoes, which are full-stack with ultra-soft max cushioning for enhanced comfort while running.

Industry observers note that there are also other Nike discounts, including 10% off for military and spouses, first responders and medical professionals, and teacher discounts after verification. Check to make sure the items you’re shopping for are covered by the discount; certain products, like Nike By You, gift cards, select launch and SNKRS products, and Apple products, are not eligible.

According to recent reports, teachers also get 10% off; just follow the steps to verify your status. All military personnel, including active, reservist, veteran, retired US military, and spouses and dependents of active personnel, also get 10% off at Nike as a thank-you for service. Plus, medical professionals and first responders are also eligible for 10% discounts; that means doctors, nurses, technicians, medical researchers, EMTs, firefighters, and law enforcement.

To get any of these discounts, you’ll need to verify with SheerID, where you’ll receive a single-use promo code that can be used once every seven days. Just be aware that the code expires after two weeks, but you can re-verify your identity to receive a new one.

According to recent reports, the Nike V5 RNR may just be the hottest everyday shoe of the season. Stylish enough for streetwear and tough enough to withstand the daily grind, this Y2K-inspired shoe features a chunky yet lightweight foam midsole. Whether you want a Nike Men’s V5 RNR, women’s, or kids’ version, the metallic details and a 3D Swoosh logo blend retro styles with modern sensibilities for an all-around solid shoe.

Nike still outfits some of the world’s top athletes. If you’re a basketball player, I’d recommend skipping the Nike Dunks and getting a pair of Kobe Protros, like Caitlin Clark. If you’re a runner, Nike recently updated the classic Pegasus. If you’re looking for a low-key street shoe that’s not an Adidas Samba, get the Nike Blazers.

There are tons of Nike’s bestselling shoes on sale right now, including: Nike Dunk Low and Dunk Low Retro SE at 24% off (with multiple under $100), Zoom Vomero 5 at 24% off, Nike Free Metcon 6 at 32% off, and custom Metcon 10 for as low as $155. Plus, classics are on sale, with Air Max 270 up to 30% off, Air Force 1 Low Retro up to 33% off, or Air Force 1 ‘07 LV8 for under $80. Be sure to check out these heavy discounts on tons of Nike styles, from classic to contemporary.

Nike got its start as a running organization, and it still makes the best running apparel on the market. My particular favorites are the firm-support, high-waisted ⅞ running leggings (because I’m short) and the running rain jacket, which is understated enough to wear as an everyday rain jacket. Sources indicate that black Friday sales are live, and while a portable power station won’t fix, well, gestures at everything, it can at least keep your phone charged when the lights go out. Portable power stations have been in high demand this year, so it's well worth shopping sale models during Black Friday.

Below, you’ll find the best Black Friday power station deals we’ve spotted so far, including Mashable-tested favorites from Anker, Bluetti, EcoFlow, and DJI.

The Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 is a Mashable fave, and for good reason. Our power station expert, Lauren Allain, gave it 4.5 stars and a Mashable Choice Award after spending two weeks using it to charge her devices and run appliances, including a rice cooker, blender, and air fryer.

It weighs just under 25 pounds and can fully recharge in 49 minutes. (You’ll need to turn on UltraFast charging in the Anker app to get that speed.) You can’t add an expansion battery, so make sure its 1,024Wh capacity works for you. But for weekend camping trips or occasional power outages, it has a lot to offer.

In a recent development, and if you missed it during October Prime Day, you’re getting another shot at the same price. The Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 is on sale for $469.99, down from $799, at Amazon. That’s a 41% discount, or $329.01 in savings.

Not everyone needs a 25-pound power station. If you’re mostly trying to keep your phone charged while you’re out and about, Allain says the Bluetti Elite 10 Mini is her “go-to” for quick trips off-grid. It weighs just four pounds, has a built-in handle, and can recharge your phone about six times.

It has been revealed that there’s also a light on the back, which she likes using as a warm nightlight in her tent. You get an AC outlet, two USB-C ports, and two USB-A ports, too, though the 128Wh battery is better suited to small devices than power-hungry appliances.

Right now, you can get the Bluetti Elite 10 Mini for $139 at Amazon, down from $199. That’s $60 off, or a 30% discount. If your packing list includes a drone, cameras, and a laptop, this one’s for you. Allain calls the DJI Power 1000 V2 a “near-perfect” portable power station for creators, especially DJI drone owners. Its dedicated ports can fast-charge compatible DJI drone batteries, but you’ll need to buy the cable separately.

It’s super quiet, so you’re not adding a bunch of fan noise to whatever you’re filming. And with four AC outlets, two USB-C ports, and two USB-A ports, there’s room for the rest of your gear. A full recharge from a wall outlet takes 56 minutes; solar charging requires a separate DJI adapter.

It has been revealed that worrying about food spoiling during a power outage is a major concern. Groceries are expensive these days, and power outages tend to always happen right after a giant Costco haul. The Jackery FridgeGuard with an expansion battery is on sale at Amazon for $260 off. Together, you'll have 2.048Wh to keep your fridge cooling for up to three hours, according to Jackery's numbers.

Unlike the standard design of most portable power stations, the Jackery FridgeGuard has a slim design, measuring 2.6 inches, so it can sit on top of your fridge, nearly invisible. The Jackery stays charged up, and it'll automatically take over when the grid fails.

Maybe we're stretching the "portable" aspect of portable power stations, but if you need more than a weekend of backup power, the EcoFlow Titan 5000 is worth the investment. Plus, it's over $1,000 off for Black Friday.

The Titan 5000 offers 5,017Wh for keeping your tech and appliances online during the next power outage. It has three standard AC ports, a TT-30R, one USB-C, and one USB-A. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Named after NBC’s iconic logo, Peacock is a video streaming service that primarily features series and film content from NBCUniversal studios, as well as news and sports programming. Premium tiers include a larger content library and access to additional NBC Sports, Hallmark Channel, and WWE content—yes, we’re talkin’ wrasslin’. Right now, you can access all those programs with a Peacock Premium subscription. Save up to 50% on your first 12 months with the latest Peacock promo codes for Black Friday and subscription deals.

With approximately 792 subscriptions, it can be hard to know exactly how much I’m paying for each (not to mention how much I’m spending each month) and which ones have the content I want to watch most. Peacock also knows that most people use several streaming services and that it’s key to choose the ones that fit best with your budget and needs. Coming in clutch when you're still in “stay-inside-and-keep-warm” mode, Peacock is offering one full year of Peacock streaming for only $80.

Recent findings suggest that one of the best ways to save on Peacock streaming is to choose the annual strategy instead of the monthly plan. The annual plan costs $80, which means you’ll get 12 months for the price of 10 and save 16% on a Premium yearly plan, for only $9 per month—otherwise it’s $11 when paid monthly. There’s also Premium Plus, which has no ads, the ability to download and watch certain titles while offline, and includes your local NBC channel live, 24/7. This subscription tier is $17 per month, or $14 when paid annually. In short, you’ll be paying only $80 annually for either Basic or Premium plans!

Recent findings suggest that being a student often means pinching pennies and eating instant ramen—we know you’re trying to save money wherever you can. With this Peacock TV student discount, eligible college students and young adults ages 18 to 24 can get a full year of Peacock Premium for just $6 a month. That’s $8 in savings per month! To claim this Peacock TV student discount, all you need to do is verify your age.

In a recent development, to unlock more discounts on a Peacock subscription, check whether you qualify for their exclusive offers for students, teachers, military members, medical workers, and other first responders. If you want Peacock for the whole family, you can stream on up to 3 devices at once and create up to 6 profiles with kid-safety settings. Peacock also offers discounts for military members and teachers – verify your status to get 12 months of Peacock Premium for $4 per month.

Sources indicate that one of the easiest ways to save on streaming services is to bundle them for a major discount. With this Apple TV and Peacock bundle, you get both services together for as little as $15 per month (essentially the price of one). You’ll save over 30% and won’t have to choose between Apple TV and Peacock. The first tier includes Apple TV and Peacock Premium, with movies, TV, Peacock originals, live sports from Peacock, and Apple originals, starting at $15 per month. The next tier, Apple TV and Peacock Premium Plus, includes all of that plus ad-free viewing and downloads, starting at $20 per month. If you already have a Peacock subscription billed directly by Peacock, you can simply sign in and upgrade to the bundle in your account.

It has been revealed that if it feels like you’re paying for about 403 streaming services, Peacock has reduced that number by one, at least. Now, you can bundle Xfinity and Peacock and save 40% on all your favorite media content for $15 per month. You can get Peacock, Apple TV+, and Netflix when you add StreamSaver with Xfinity Internet. Prices vary by proposal: Netflix with ads is $8 per month, Peacock Premium with ads is $8 per month, and the Peacock Apple TV+ bundle is $15 per month.

There’s a wide range of upcoming content coming to Peacock this month, including some new releases for reality TV fans like me. Some of the newest content coming to Peacock includes horror-comedy Five Nights at Freddy's 2, the sequel to the animatronic original nightmare. Plus, rejoice because baseball season is here, and you can catch up on the action by streaming MLB games on Peacock, including Sunday Night Baseball, MLB Sunday Leadoff, and the thrilling Postseason Wild Card Round.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re like me and love to absolutely turn your brain off (I’m talking no neuron flare-ups would be detected in an MRI) and watch reality TV, let me introduce you to the wonderful world of Love Island. If you love watching Instagram models go from room to room, to the pool, to the gym, and back again in a long-form version of a game of Telephone, this is the show for you. The great part is that every episode is about an hour long, and there are approximately 4,200 episodes per season.

Sources indicate that if you’re caught up on the latest Love Island drama, get stoked for their newest spin-off, Love Island: Beyond the Villa, where the clueless cast from the latest season tries to attempt the impossible challenge of juggling multiple social media brand endorsements. It’s a real nail-biter.

Recent findings suggest that basketball season is upon us again, and Peacock is likely the most reliable way to catch all your favorite NBA teams. Basketball fans, you’re in luck: 100 regular-season games are now available on NBC and Peacock, along with NBA playoff games, the Conference Finals, the NBA All-Star Game, and Monday games and Tuesday night doubleheaders throughout the regular season. Note that the basic "Select" subscription tier doesn't include live sports, but Plus and Premium do. Be sure to check the NBA schedule on Peacock and NBC for the full lineup.

Sources indicate that if I’m being honest, one of the biggest reasons I have Peacock is its NFL coverage, including Sunday Night Football and playoff games. (Yes, I love Love Island and football; I contain multitudes.) After living across the country, I like to regularly watch the Chiefs, Bills, Niners, Raiders, Lions, and Chargers to keep up with the fandoms I’ve become part of. Trying to find where to watch Sunday Night Football was a headache, but now I can have the substantial game in my living room. (Now I’m just wondering when technology will catch up and bring Jalen Hurts into my living room as well.) Sports fans rejoice because Peacock often gets exclusive streaming rights to specific games. For example, last NFL season, Peacock was the place to stream the Week 1 game.

Like other streaming services, Peacock offers looks for every type of binge-watcher. Their subscription tiers let you customize based on what you’ll actually watch and your budget: Select, for $8 per month; Premium, for $11 per month, which includes Peacock’s catalog, live sports, current NBC and Bravo shows, and over 50 channels. Premium Plus is $17 per month or $170 per year and includes: no ads, the ability to download titles to watch offline, and access to your local NBC channel live 24/7. Peacock Premium includes over 80k hours of streaming, with newly introduced and old shows, films, and originals, live sports, presently running NBC and Bravo shows (OG Real Housewives fans know), and over 50 channels that are always streaming something. The Premium Plus initiative includes everything I just mentioned, plus no ads (a huge W for people who chronically get on their phones during commercials and forget to pay attention when the show comes back on). Check out the full details on the different Peacock plans to figure out which is right for you.

Industry observers note that not sure what gift to get for your next celebration? A Peacock gift card gives your loved one over 80,000 hours of TV, movies, and sports. You can get a digital gift card right on Peacock’s website and send it to a recipient via email or text, with no cumbersome shipping required. With a Peacock gift card, you can pay for a Peacock streaming initiative using the “Redeem Gift Card” button on the checkout page. If you’ve already made a Peacock account, you can add the gift card on your Account page. Once you’ve added the Peacock gift card to your account, you’ll be able to see the credit balance, and it will be applied to your subscription until it runs out.

A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1336 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As artificial intelligence becomes an unavoidable part of everyday life and models become ever more sophisticated, the cost of the energy required to run the technology is ballooning.
  • Recent findings suggest that to rein in runaway costs, AI labs and cloud providers are trying to build fresh data centers in places with cheap and plentiful renewable energy—like Scandinavia.
  • An expanding field of hardware startups, among them German company Q.ANT, is coming at the problem from a different direction: by developing a new breed of chip—photonic processors—meant to minimize the amount of energy that AI models consume.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As artificial intelligence becomes an unavoidable part of everyday life and models become ever more sophisticated, the cost of the energy required to run the technology is ballooning.

Recent findings suggest that to rein in runaway costs, AI labs and cloud providers are trying to build fresh data centers in places with cheap and plentiful renewable energy—like Scandinavia. But logistical challenges, a scarcity of key components, and a swell of anti-data center protests are getting in the way.

An expanding field of hardware startups, among them German company Q.ANT, is coming at the problem from a different direction: by developing a new breed of chip—photonic processors—meant to minimize the amount of energy that AI models consume.

Whereas regular GPUs transmit and process data by shuffling electrons around, photonic processors use waves of light. Because light doesn’t generate heat as it travels and allows more data to be processed simultaneously, photonic processors supposedly consume less energy and require minimal cooling—one of the largest sources of cost for data centers.

According to recent reports, the aim isn’t to replace GPUs with photonic processors, but to run them side-by-side. Whilst GPUs excel at grinding through masses of additions and multiplications—linear math—photonic processors are best suited to complex, nonlinear calculations.

According to recent reports, few photonic processors are running inside data centers today. But Q.ANT recently rolled out its chips to facilities operated by cloud manufacturer IONOS as part of a pilot program. It says that more than 30 teams of engineers are now developing AI models optimized for photonic computing.

Earlier this month, WIRED spoke with Michael Förtsch, founder and CEO of Q.ANT. We discussed the energy bottlenecks constraining AI development, how photonic processors differ from regular chips, and the challenges Q.ANT faces in trying to popularize a newly introduced class of hardware.

This conversation has been edited for length and clarity.

WIRED: Michael, could you start by outlining the problem Q.ANT is aiming to solve? Why does the world need photonic processors to run AI models?

Michael Förtsch: The overall problem is the cost generated by the huge amount of energy consumption.

If you compute the way we think light should be used—not as a direct replacement for a GPU, but as a coprocessor—you basically have a new processor that takes care of the heavy math.

Industry observers note that the cost driver today is the access to the memory. The less data you need in order to complete a job, the more efficient and better your system. We execute complicated math in a single step, where [regular chips] need thousands of steps. This saves a bunch of data—or memory access points.

According to recent reports, how would you explain to the layperson how photonic computing works? How can light be used to perform mathematical computations?

Light is a wave. What is a wave? A sine function. [The sine function is a mathematical rule that, when plotted to a graph, produces a smooth repeating wave. —Editor] If I want to model something that’s round in shape with only linear functions, I need an infinite amount of data points and lines in order to describe something very simple: a circle. If I have the sine function at hand, because light is a wave, I need two points and I have already described the circle in all its beauty.

Light is very, very gifted to operate on complicated equations.

What distinguishes the type of problem best left to regular chips from problems that should be delegated to photonic processors?

According to recent reports, the Nvidia H200 GPU is a masterpiece of technology. It’s art. It’s truly hard to attack it in its homeground. But light has strengths where the GPU is weak—and vice versa.

Sources indicate that linear math? Please route it to the GPU. Non-linear and complex stuff? Please route it to us.

We believe we will be much stronger in everything related to pictures and videos: image recognition, segmentation, and generation. Then, everything that’s related to robotics and physical AI.

What is the estimated gain in energy efficiency tied to using photonic processors alongside GPUs for AI tasks?

In a recent development, I’m not saying photonic computing will come for free. But I see that photonic computing, in combination with [CPUs and GPUs], can bring you a lot more artificial intelligence at a fraction of the energy.

Under simulation, we are ending up at around four or five times energy reduction. But in real hardware we are not yet demonstrating it.

Can any task run on photonic hardware by default, or do they need to be configured in a certain way?

According to recent reports, there’s no need to learn a different language than C++ or Python. And you can already execute [preexisting] code on our machines.

In a recent development, but if you take something that has been optimized for a GPU only, you should not expect that automatically things will run faster. You have to do some adaptations.

It’s a chicken and egg problem, right? Until developers are building models to run on this type of processor, it’s going to be difficult to sell them to cloud providers. Equally, until photonic processors are available for people to use, it’s going to be tough to convince developers to design for them.

Whether it’s photonic or any other processor technology, it will need time to get the credibility and trust that’s needed for a company like Google to build data center infrastructure around it.

That’s the reason we chose to go into data centers with proof of concept systems, to validate that photonic computing is robust enough to withstand that environment.

It has been revealed that we want to invite the world to compute on our systems. We are building a fresh chicken, so you can start producing eggs. Let’s find out together whether they’re tasty or not.

What else should I understand about why photonic processors are not already widely in use?

If hypothetically we received an order of 100,000 [photonic processors], we at Q.ANT are ready, but I’m not sure about the suppliers.

It has been revealed that hardware is not software. On the assembly side, it will need [time] before we have the same robust supply chain as the semiconductor world.

Do you expect to suffer from the same problem as other hardware challengers in securing capacity with the big chip manufacturers?

Industry observers note that [To produce Q.ANT chips] you only need 90 nanometer node technology, from the 2000s. A lot of foundries already use this capability to produce chips that are super cheap. With this technology, you can use the same line to produce high-performance chips with a much higher street price, without massive upfront investment in your assets.

That resonates well with the industry.

Are Q.ANT processors built to function alongside a particular brand of GPUs—say, Nvidia or AMD—or are they totally agnostic?

In a recent development, there’s no need to go single-sided with a particular GPU. We want to have the freedom to cooperate with any of them.

Either way, we are not competitive to GPUs, we complete their function set.

Can you imagine a future in which AI models run entirely on photonic processors, or will they always be a sidekick?

If we see an opportunity in five years to attack the GPU as well, we would not be shy about taking it. But at the same time, I do not know what workloads in five years are going to be like.

It depends on the architecture of future AI models, you mean?

Could the chance to perform certain calculations more cheaply with photonic processors change the way that AI engineers design future models?

The core message is that we need to do something to fight the energy cost in the AI stack.

That’s where we see the future of AI: very data-optimized models that allow for tasks of the same quality, but at a fraction of the energy—and therefore a fraction of the operating cost.

Black Friday deals are coming in hot and heavy. We're inundated with fresh price drops on laptops, headphones, fitness trackers, and everything in between. And yes, we're seeing a huge number of price drops on Apple.

Industry observers note that wading through the deals on iPads, MacBooks, and AirPods, it's tough to ignore T-Mobile's massive sale on iPhones. If you've been waiting until now to upgrade, you're in luck: For limited-time, the Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free at T-Mobile. Yes, you read that right.

In a recent development, T-Mobile keeps things surprisingly flexible when it comes to qualifying for this Black Friday deal. You can port your existing phone number from an eligible rival carrier to a qualifying T-Mix plan, and T-Mobile covers the full cost of the phone. Alternatively, existing customers can trade in an eligible phone in any condition on a qualifying T-Mix plan.

Industry observers note that T-Mobile distributes the full discount as 36 monthly bill credits. If you leave T-Mobile or cancel your line before that three-year payment initiative ends, the credits stop immediately, and you will owe the remaining balance on the device.

Sources indicate that you are also still required to pay local sales tax on the phone's full $1,199 retail value upfront, plus T-Mobile's standard $35 device connection fee per line at checkout. Unfortunately, you can't escape those upfront charges.

Score the Apple iPhone 18 Pro for free with T-Mobile over Black Friday.

Why not take a break from your uncle’s MAGA monolog, put down your turkey-laden fork, and embrace a more modern American Thanksgiving tradition: shopping for the best Black Friday deals. This weekend used to be about retailers dumping old stock at big discounts to make room for the upcoming, but now the deals on tech come thick and fast, often on the latest gear (though it’s not always clear which discounts are real).

Welcome to WIRED’s guide to the best Black Friday tech deals. I can promise you that everything here is worth buying (we’ve tested and recommended all of it), and these are real discounts (not the year-round price). If you need an upgrade, a pick-me-up, or some great techy gifts, you’re in the right place. For more Black Friday deals, check out our other guides, like the Best Black Friday TV Deals or the Best Black Friday Mattress Deals.

It has been revealed that perhaps the most exciting release of the year (unless you're an Apple person), the Z Fold8 is our top pick of the best folding phones. Samsung’s experience demonstrates with a fresh form factor that feels revelatory. Both the 5.5-inch cover screen and the 7.7-inch inner screen are bright, sharp, and genuinely useful. There's a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset and plenty of stamina, thanks to the 4,800-mAh silicon-carbon battery. A $350 discount brings it to the lowest price we’ve seen yet.

Sources indicate that after testing many, many Apple 3-in-1 wireless chargers, this is the one that claimed a permanent place on my bedside table. It looks classy, and I love the weighted base, enabling you to grab your iPhone without pulling the whole charger off the nightstand. The pad also tilts and holds your iPhone vertically or horizontally, with support for StandBy mode. It can fast-charge capable iPhone and Apple Watch models and charge any AirPods with a wireless charging case. The 5-foot braided cable is permanently attached, and there’s a 36-watt wall charger in the box.

Handy as they are for keeping you connected when your phone dies unexpectedly, portable chargers can be very same-y. One of the reasons the Nimble Champ is in our Best Power Banks guide is Nimble’s focus on the environment. It’s made from 90 percent certified recycled plastic and comes in fully biodegradable packaging. It also works well, with capacities starting from 5,200 mAh, with USB-A and USB-C ports, and up to 15-watt charging.

While it's no longer my top pick of the best travel adapters, this is still a solid option and will keep all of your gadgetry running wherever you travel. There's a classic slider design for the plug that covers more than 200 countries, but you also get one USB-C port, two USB-A ports, and a handy retractable USB-C cable (perfect if you're forgetful).

It has been revealed that it’s the thoughtful design that elevates the Backbone One above the rest of the best mobile controllers out there. Slot your phone into the compact cradle, with a USB-C jack for speedy connectivity, and you get satisfyingly clicky and responsive controls plus a 3.5-mm headphone port. You can also customize it for different games, or even use Backbone’s software as a one-stop gaming hub (if you’re willing to pay a subscription).

In a recent development, if you want a virtual screen for gaming that you can take anywhere, the Viture Beast XR are my favorite smart glasses for gaming. These glasses can plug directly into your phone (and many other gadgets) via USB-C to give you a bright 174-inch virtual screen. It's also worth snagging the excellent 8BitDo controller. If these are still too pricey, the Viture Luma Pro for $339 ($160 off) are a good alternative.

Already the cheapest Apple laptop, an extra $50 off the MacBook Neo is not to be sneezed at. In fact, it's a great deal for anyone seeking an affordable laptop that feels premium, with a metal chassis and quality display. The limited 8 GB of RAM is a definite compromise, but for folks with modest needs, the MacBook Neo should serve just fine.

Industry observers note that don't ask me why they keep taking away our ports. God forbid you should want to plug something into your laptop. Well, you can stick it to those minimalist designers with one of the best laptop docks. Despite the small size, this one boasts powerful ports, including 96-watt power delivery and support for up to three 4K displays at a time (or a single 4K monitor at 120 Hz using the USB-C port). The card slots, USB, and headphone jack are up front, with the display, power, and Ethernet ports around back.

The Asus RT-BE58U is perhaps the ideal Wi-Fi 7 upgrade for modest homes and apartments still struggling with the crappy router their internet service provider sent, and that's why it tops our Best Wi-Fi Routers guide. It’s easy to set up and use, can cover up to 2,000 square feet, and has plenty of ports. As a dual-band router, it lacks the 6-GHz band, but it has all the other advantages of Wi-Fi 7. There’s also support for VPN service, separate IoT or guest networks, and Ai Mesh.

According to recent reports, we love Amazon's Eero mesh systems for being easy to set up and use, but they also double as smart home hubs with support for Matter, Thread, and Zigbee. The Eero Pro 7 is a tri-band mesh router that adds the 6-GHz band to the familiar 2.4-GHz and 5-GHz bands. For busy households with many devices and a 1-Gbps or faster connection, this mesh system is ideal. Just bear in mind that the 6-GHz band is short-range. The pricey Eero Plus subscription is an extra $10 per month (or $100 per year), but it adds a ton of value with parental controls, advanced security, ad blocking, and even a password manager and VPN service.

This is a rare and tasty deal on my favorite Xmas lights. They work indoors or out, can be scheduled, and support a bunch of lovely animated effects. While I'm on the topic of Philips Hue and its excellent but horribly expensive lights, you might want to check out some of its other Black Friday deals (I would go for the wall washers and the TV lightstrip).

It has been revealed that you know what I don't miss? Mowing the lawn. A good robot mower, like this relatively affordable one from TerraMow, will do it for you, quietly. No wire required; it recharges itself. You just set a schedule and relax. OK, it sometimes leaves a verge, but the only model I've tried that doesn't is more than twice the price.

It has been revealed that these wireless noise-canceling headphones may not be the latest release from Sony, but they are still an excellent pair of cans with a far deeper discount. The Sony WH-1000XM5 are relatively light and comfortable, producing accomplished sound in every scenario, and have great control options.

According to recent reports, the JBL Flip 7 is the Bluetooth speaker that has it all. It's durable, it has stamina, it produces a punchy sound, and it comes in fun colors. As the best Bluetooth speaker you can buy, this deal is for real.

Yes, you should read more, and Amazon’s Kindle e-readers make it easier to do just that. Our current favorite is the Kindle Paperwhite (12th generation). It has a sharp 7-inch display, auto-adjusting warm light, three-month battery life, and snappy performance, and it’s slim and light. It even has integration with Overdrive for your library books and support for several languages.

Sources indicate that our favorite budget Android tablet has a 12.2-inch, 2400 x 1600 pixel LCD panel that’s sharp, colorful, and bright, with a 120-Hz refresh rate. It's perfect for web browsing or kicking back with a movie or sports game, but the aging Qualcomm Snapdragon 4 Gen 2 chipset makes it not the best option for gamers.

This deal on LG’s 65-inch C6 OLED TV caught my eye. At 48 percent off the regular price, this is the cheapest it has ever been, making it a better option than the entry-level LG B6 we just reviewed. Just make sure you pair it with a streaming device and disable the tracking. There are similar discounts on most of the other sizes of this TV.

Industry observers note that released this year, the Samsung S95H OLED TV has never been priced lower than this. This TV promises accurate color and deep blacks. It also sports a snazzy silver bezel that’s recessed behind the main OLED panel that resembles a metal picture frame.

Sources indicate that up your home theater game with a surround sound system from Sony. The Bravia Theater System 6 has a classy, understated design, combining a beefy subwoofer, two tall and musical surround speakers, and a small center soundbar to envelop you in audio. It's a great way to get more from your movies.

That's because myriad products have seen price increases in 2026 due to factors like higher fuel costs, tariffs, and the ongoing memory shortage, aka "RAMageddon.".

The latter is the reason why Amazon raised the prices of its Kindle e-readers, Fire TV Sticks, and most Echo smart speakers in August.

Amazon's Black Friday sale isn't exclusive to Prime members. This is one of the main things that separates it from other Amazon events like Prime Day and Prime Significant Deal Days.

The British Government is Turning Everyone Into a Prepper

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in 2010, the UK experienced one of its coldest ever winters, with heavy snowfall bringing major roads to a standstill.
  • Industry observers note that next time, Brian decided, he would be prepared.
  • Preppers generally operate on the fringe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in 2010, the UK experienced one of its coldest ever winters, with heavy snowfall bringing major roads to a standstill. Brian, an engineer in central Scotland, had little food in the house. He donned a backpack, took one of his children’s sledges, and trudged a mile and half to queue outside the nearest supermarket. Shelves were emptying, and tempers were fraying.

Industry observers note that next time, Brian decided, he would be prepared. “It’s very hard to look your kids in the eye when you’re looking at a relatively empty cupboard,” he indicates. Brian started building up a store of non-perishable food and other supplies, ready for unexpected shortages. He’s now part of the UK’s prepper community—a group of survivalists who proposal proactively for emergency situations such as natural disasters or infrastructure breakdowns. He shares his tips on YouTube as Scottishprepper73; he reckons his family could live a full year off his stash.

Preppers generally operate on the fringe. They’re used to people considering them crazy and paranoid. When Brian tells friends about his plans, they often respond with jokes. Or worse, they tell him “I’ll just come to your house.” Then, last month, the UK government introduced its “Be Ready” campaign, which advised households to stock up on three days’ worth of bottled water, tinned food, and other essentials. The advice, the Cabinet Office stated, was “the first stage of a three-year campaign to help households across the UK feel better prepared for events such as severe weather, which can occasionally affect services including power, water, phones and the internet.”.

Prepping was flung into the mainstream, and British preppers—a minority in a largely US-dominated scene—have found themselves drawn out of their (metaphorical) bunkers and into the limelight.

For the most part, preppers I spoke to welcomed the government advice, though they unanimously felt it didn't go far enough (“What’s your plan for day four?” Mike Chappell, a Greater Manchester-based prepper, says.) But public reactions, they say, have been mixed.

According to recent reports, dan Goss, who is based in Liverpool and runs the Start Prepping UK website, notes traffic to his site “went bananas,” reaching around 50,000 visitors at one point. The news, he says, has “broken people’s normalcy bias,” legitimising the idea of prepping in a way that no amount of bleak climate news can. He’s observed a rise in what he calls the “normal person prepper”—people who aren’t interested in planning for an apocalypse or learning advanced survival skills, but want to build basic household resilience. Glyn Smith, founder of the prepper community UK Survival Network, reports a similar spike in interest. “It’s not lone survivalists; it’s mums, dads, couples, and retirees,” he says. “Normal people who want practical peace of mind.”.

Dan recommends: In terms of hardware or capabilities it’s hard to beat a Sawyer Mini water filter. They’re tiny, lightweight, need no energy source to run, and can filter something like 100,000 liters of water before they need to be replaced.

Recent findings suggest that there’s also been pushback. Every time prepping hits the news, Brian says, some people respond with aggression. When he’s spoken to media before, multiple people have made death threats. “‘I’m not going to waste money on preps, I’ll just buy a shotgun and come to your house,’ yada yada,” he says. For this reason, he, and several other preppers I spoke to, asked to be identified only by their first name. As well as hostility, Goss says, some people complain that they can’t afford to prep, or that the government should provide. A common sentiment, Chappell says, is that “nothing ever happens anyway.” Some accuse preppers of fearmongering.

Sources indicate that the general image of the prepping community probably doesn’t help. Think “prepper” and you might imagine a caricature of a man in camo and armed to the teeth, either hunkering down in a nuclear bunker or camping out in the wilderness. But the preppers I speak to present a much more mundane, inclusive, and, well, British approach to prepping. They are keen to distance themselves from the idea of the “doomsday prepper.” Instead, they prep for less extreme but more likely incidents. As the UK anticipates winter weather buffeted by an El Niño climate pattern, they worry about storms, floods, and crop failures. Something as simple as a burst water pipe or power cut could cause localized chaos. Then there’s the threat of cyberattacks: Just this month, supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe were hacked in an attack France believes was conducted by Iran.

Glyn recommends: A Lifesaver bottle or Lifesaver Jerrycan and an EcoFlow power station such as the Delta 3.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, indicates Ana, a prepper based in south Wales, the impacts are likely to be the same. “It’s going to be affecting potentially your food supply in the supermarkets, your water, your electricity,” she says. Ana has a food channel on YouTube, but pivoted to prepper content when she realized most people had no idea how to preserve food for long-term storage. She grew up growing food, cooking from scratch, and keeping a full pantry, and has maintained these habits. The Covid-19 pandemic reminded her just how vulnerable the UK supply chain is. She was pregnant at the time and noticed a shortage of baby formula; a supermarket worker told her people had been buying it to put in their coffee and tea.

It’s always a good idea to keep a store of basics like bottled water and long-life food. True preppers often invest in more specialized items. Brian gives me a virtual tour of the shed where he stores his supplies, neatly arranged in floor-to-ceiling shelving units. He points to different types of water filtration kits, including a LifeSaver Jerrycan capable of purifying up to 20,000 liters, and rattles off medical supplies (“Antibiotics, tourniquets, chest seals, splints”). He has a few different cooking setups, such as foldable stoves that use gas canisters, and keeps buckets of freeze-dried food that will last for 25 years. Next door, he tells me, there are 165 gallons of fresh water that he refreshes every six months.

Industry observers note that brian recommends: A reasonably sized power bank such as a Bluetti Elite 300, which will give you days of backup power for your home. Add in some solar panels and you have a two-to-three-year renewable power source.

In a recent development, many preppers prepare to go off-grid if the power and internet fail, but Brian has staked his bets on a tech-heavy setup. He has a generator, his house is fitted out with solar panels, and he uses an air source heat pump for heating. He has a backup heater that runs on diesel, and several extremely powerful portable power stations (think a rechargeable power bank, but with enough capacity to keep appliances like a microwave going). He uses Starlink for internet access and runs two different mesh networking systems, with high-frequency radio acting as his ultimate fallback. In his shed, he has plenty of torches, lanterns, candles, radios, walkie-talkies, and a night-vision headset. The way he sees it, you might be able to survive without power, but it wouldn’t be much fun. “We’ve got enough tech these days that life doesn’t have to be uncomfortable,” Brian states.

It has been revealed that this is a key difference between the US and UK prepper scenes: While many US preppers proposal to “bug out” and live alone off-grid, British preppers mainly plan to stay at home. “We don’t have that vast wilderness to escape to,” says Chappell, who makes content as the UK Urban Prepper and keeps most of his at-home supplies stacked in what used to be the dining room. When we speak, Chappell has a four-week-old daughter, so his stocks include enough formula milk to get her to solid foods. Nappies are too bulky to stockpile en masse, but he has enough for a short-term glitch and a fallback of old-fashioned terry towel nappies.

Mike recommends: My number one would be any kind of water filter. I love the Grayl one for simplicity.

Sources indicate that while prepping is often depicted as a lone wolf activity, British preppers are, on the whole, more community-minded. The scene in general has a degree of secrecy around it; some preppers keep their preps tightly under wraps out of fears that, if people know what they have, they could become a target.

It has been revealed that goss dismisses fears of people turning on each other in a crisis. He evokes a sense of Blitz spirit: when times get tough, he suggests, people tend to come together rather than pull apart. In any case, he doesn’t really have a choice. Like Chappell, he lives in a terraced house in an urban area—a far shout from a private bunker. “Like it or not, you’re going to wind up working with your neighbors during a big giant blackout event or something,” he indicates. “And it would be a really good idea for you to kind of plan for that ahead of time.” He suggests gaining trust by setting up a street WhatsApp group and doing small favors for neighbors. In an emergency scenario, pooling resources and knowledge may be more effective than going it alone. And if things did descend into looting and fighting–well, wouldn’t you want your neighbors on side?

Ana recommends: A power station like Allpowers’ R1500, an Aferiy 2400w station, or the Ecoworthy PS2400. All have great capacity and multiple charging options.

Recent findings suggest that others thought this view might be too optimistic. “When you’re bombarded with information 24/7 and you’re deprived of any information in a general power cut, it wouldn’t take long before people get nervous and start to do stupid things because they panic,” Brian states. “You get a fear response. Fear leads to poor choices, potentially fatal ones.” He’s thought about what he’d do if friends really did turn up on his doorstep like they joke about. “It’s a difficult one,” he says. “I don’t have an answer.”.

It has been revealed that in that kind of scenario, Chappell has a initiative to bug out, but just to a family member’s home. His house is surrounded by people he doesn’t know, and he can’t predict how they might react. It’s not that he doesn’t want to help people, he says, but he’s not willing to risk his family’s safety.

In a recent development, of course, these intends go well beyond a three-day water-and-beans buffer. For many of the people I speak to, prepping is also a hobby. There are meet-ups and workshops. Goss states he enjoys camping and tending his allotment—activities that fit neatly into the prepper skillset (he’s also into archery, just to complete the image). But still, it’s nice to be ready, just in case. “This is not a way of life where I sit in a bunker hoping for the sky to fall. I want nothing ever to happen,” Chappell says. “But it’s insurance, right?”.

Latest Update: Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (697 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the most enticing features of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) is the incredibly well-realized worlds, especially among the most recent installments in the franchise.
  • Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA is one of the most valuable intellectual properties in the video game industry.
  • Recent findings suggest that like the recently released game—which is so detailed you can even go birding in it—GTA V is a meticulous recreation of the real world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most enticing features of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) is the incredibly well-realized worlds, especially among the most recent installments in the franchise. In this detailed rendering, researchers saw an unusual opportunity: What if these video games could be used to model the effects of the climate crisis?

Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA is one of the most valuable intellectual properties in the video game industry. As of this year, the franchise has sold an estimated 465 million units worldwide, and the latest installment in the series, GTA VI, earned $3.79 billion in first-day sales.

Recent findings suggest that like the recently released game—which is so detailed you can even go birding in it—GTA V is a meticulous recreation of the real world. It’s setting, Los Santos, is a fictional city inspired by Los Angeles and consists of pretty much the same topographical, urban, and coastal features of the Californian metropolis.

These specs were leveraged by Paul Nörenberg, a professor at the University of Potsdam in Germany, and his colleague Hugues Lantuit of the Alfred Wegener Institute, who conducted an experiment to determine whether the video game could serve as a useful tool for projecting the severity and impact of flooding and sea-level rise under various future scenarios related to global warming.

Industry observers note that the authors of the study, published in Geoscience Communication, created a digital model based on the video game’s three-dimensional terrain maps. This allowed them to estimate which areas of Los Santos would be submerged if sea levels continue to rise.

The researchers calculated these possibilities based on two climate scenarios used in the projections of the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).

In a recent development, the first, known as RCP 2.6, assumes that countries implement effective measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. The second, called RCP 8.5, envisions a scenario of high emissions without sufficient mitigation measures. In both cases, the authors made projections of potential climate impacts for the years 2100, 2300, and 2500, and included simulations of storm surges.

In a recent development, the results revealed that, in a high-emissions scenario and in the event of a storm surge, sea-level rise and coastal flooding could reach 5.18 meters by 2300. The model estimates that, under these conditions, 5.1 percent of Los Santos’ land area would be flooded, affecting the port, wastewater treatment facilities, and coastal energy infrastructure.

In a recent development, estimates for the same scenario, but for the year 2500, project that the combined water level would reach 8.22 meters and that 6.5 percent of the land area would be submerged. In contrast, under the emissions-reduction scenario, flooding would affect only 2.2 percent of the territory by 2300, without impacting major infrastructure.

In a second phase, the researchers sought to verify whether the simulations based on the GTA V map could reflect what would happen in the real city. To do so, they compared the results of their model with scientific data on the areas of Los Angeles most vulnerable to flooding. The comparison revealed that the areas identified as vulnerable in the video game coincided with the three locations in the real city most likely to experience flooding: Venice Beach, Pacific Palisades, and the Port of Los Angeles.

“This congruence supports the conclusion that the GTA V terrain is sufficiently faithful to real-world morphology to be scientifically meaningful,” the authors write. The researchers caution, however, that their results should not be interpreted as an exact prediction, since the GTA V model and maps do not account for all possible real-world phenomena that influence flood risk, including wave motion, beach erosion, currents, or changes in terrain.

It has been revealed that the researchers also see a benefit from using GTA V to model climate effects that extends beyond the results themselves. Not only does Los Santos look like the real world, but millions of people have spent countless hours exploring it. For the connection many have to these games, a climate model based in this simulation might feel closer to reality.

This story originally appeared on WIRED en Español and has been translated from Spanish.
